bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第169卷卷第一百六十九

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 169, the one hundred sixty-ninth fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 169.

sentences.zh: 【陳紀三】 起昭陽協洽，盡柔兆閹茂，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Chen Records 3] Beginning with Zhaoyang Xiehe, ending with Rouzhao Yanmao, four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Chen Annals 3] Spanning from the year Zhaoyang Xiehe through Rouzhao Yanmao—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，齊以太子少傅魏收兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Qi made the Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, Wei Shou, also Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Northern Qi appointed Wei Shou, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, to serve concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時齊主終日酣飲，朝事專委侍中高元海。

translations.literal: At this time the ruler of Qi drank heavily all day long, and court affairs were entrusted entirely to Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler spent his days in drunken revelry, leaving state affairs wholly in the hands of Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Yuanhai.

sentences.zh: 元海庸俗，帝亦輕之；

translations.literal: Yuanhai was vulgar and commonplace, and the emperor also looked down on him;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai was a mediocrity, and the emperor held him in low regard;

sentences.zh: 以收才名素盛，故用之。

translations.literal: Because Wei Shou's literary reputation had long been great, he was appointed for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was given the post only because his literary fame was already well established.

sentences.zh: 而收畏懦避事，尋坐阿縱，除名。

translations.literal: But Wei Shou was timid and avoided responsibility; shortly thereafter he was convicted of indulgence and stripped of his name from office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, however, proved timid and shirked his duties; before long he was convicted of complicity in wrongdoing and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史畢義雲作書與高元海，論敘時事。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Bi Yiyun wrote a letter to Gao Yuanhai discussing and narrating current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yiyun, inspector of Yanzhou, wrote to Gao Yuanhai setting out his views on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 元海入宮，不覺遺之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai entered the palace and unknowingly left it behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai went into the palace and left the letter behind without realizing it.

sentences.zh: 給事中李孝貞得而奏之，帝由是疏元海。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Xiaozhen obtained it and submitted it; by this the emperor became distant toward Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Xiaozhen found the letter and reported it to the throne, and from that time the emperor kept Yuanhai at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 以孝貞兼中書舍人，征義雲還朝。

translations.literal: Li Xiaozhen was made concurrent Secretariat Drafter, and Bi Yiyun was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaozhen was appointed concurrent Secretariat Drafter, and Bi Yiyun was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 和士開復譖元海，帝以馬鞭棰元海六十，責曰：「汝昔教我反，以弟反兄，幾許不義！

translations.literal: He Shikai again slandered Yuanhai; the emperor beat Yuanhai sixty times with a riding crop and rebuked him, saying: "You once urged me to rebel—using a younger brother to rebel against an elder brother, how very unrighteous!
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai slandered Yuanhai again. The emperor lashed him sixty strokes with a riding crop and upbraided him: "You once urged me to rebel—having a younger brother turn against his elder brother: how shameless can one be!

sentences.zh: 以鄴城兵抗并州，幾許無智！」

translations.literal: Using the troops of Ye to resist Bingzhou—how very witless!"
translations.idiomatic: Pitting the army of Ye against Bingzhou—how foolish was that!"

sentences.zh: 出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to serve as inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，周迪眾潰，脫身逾嶺，奔晉安，依陳寶應。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Zhou Di's forces collapsed; he escaped over the mountains and fled to Jin'an, placing himself under Chen Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, Zhou Di's army broke and scattered. He slipped over the mountains to Jin'an and threw in his lot with Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 官軍克臨川，獲迪妻子。

translations.literal: The government army captured Linchuan and took Zhou Di's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces took Linchuan and captured Zhou Di's family.

sentences.zh: 寶應以兵資迪，留異又遣其子忠臣隨之。

translations.literal: Baoying supplied troops to support Di, and Liu Yi also sent his son Zhongchen to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying furnished Zhou Di with troops, and Liu Yi sent his son Zhongchen to join him as well.

sentences.zh: 虞寄與寶應書，以十事諫之曰：「自天厭梁德，英雄互起，人人自以為得之，然夷凶翦亂，四海樂推者，陳氏也。

translations.literal: Yu Ji wrote to Baoying, admonishing him with ten points, saying: "Since Heaven grew weary of the Liang dynasty's virtue, heroes rose one after another, each believing he would win the prize; yet the one who quelled the barbarians, cut down disorder, and was joyfully acclaimed by all within the four seas was the house of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji wrote Chen Baoying a letter of remonstrance in ten points, saying: "Since Heaven had turned against the virtue of Liang, heroes sprang up everywhere, each convinced that the mandate was his—yet the house that pacified the savage lands, ended the turmoil, and won the willing allegiance of the realm was Chen.

sentences.zh: 豈非歷數有在，惟天所授乎！

translations.literal: Is this not because the succession of fate has its appointed place, granted by Heaven alone?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because the mandate had its ordained holder, bestowed by Heaven alone?

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is the first point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first point.

sentences.zh: 以王琳之強，侯瑱之力，進足以搖蕩中原，爭衡天下，退足以屈強江外，雄張偏隅；

translations.literal: With Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power, advancing they were sufficient to shake the Central Plains and contend for the empire; retreating they were sufficient to bend the mighty south of the Yangzi and dominate a corner of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin at his height and Hou Tian in his prime could advance far enough to shake the heartland and vie for the empire, or fall back and still cow the strong south of the Yangzi and lord it over a distant quarter;

sentences.zh: 然或命一旅之師，或資一士之說，琳則瓦解冰泮，投身異域，瑱則闕角稽顙，委命闕庭，斯又天假之威而除其患。

translations.literal: Yet whether by dispatching a single brigade or relying on the counsel of one scholar, Lin then dissolved like ice melting, casting himself into a foreign land, while Tian bowed with broken horn at the court gate and entrusted his fate to the imperial palace—this again was Heaven lending its majesty to remove their threat.
translations.idiomatic: yet whether Chen sent a single brigade or heeded one man's counsel, Lin's power melted like ice in spring and he ended his days in exile, while Tian came to court with horns lowered and submitted his fate at the palace steps—again Heaven lent its authority to sweep their menace away.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: This is the second point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second point.

sentences.zh: 今將軍以籓戚之重，東南之眾，盡忠奉上，戮力勤王，豈不勳高竇融，寵過吳芮，析珪判野，南面稱孤乎！

translations.literal: Now, General, with the weight of an imperial kinsman by marriage and the hosts of the southeast, if you devote your loyalty to the throne and join your strength to serve the dynasty, would your merit not surpass Dou Rong's, your favor exceed Wu Rui's, with fiefs carved out and a realm of your own, facing south as a sovereign in your own right?
translations.idiomatic: Today, General, you bear the weight of an imperial marriage alliance and command the armies of the southeast. If you gave your full loyalty to the throne and threw your strength into the emperor's service, would your merit not outshine Dou Rong's, your honors exceed Wu Rui's—with domains carved out for you and the right to rule your own quarter as a great prince of the realm?

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is the third point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third point.

sentences.zh: 聖朝棄瑕忘過，寬厚得人，至於余孝頃、潘純陀、李孝欽、歐陽頠等，悉委以心腹，任以爪牙，腦中豁然，曾無纖芥。

translations.literal: The sacred court overlooks flaws and forgets past offenses, winning men through magnanimity. As for Yu Xiaoqing, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Hui, and the like, all were entrusted as intimate confidants and employed as claws and fangs, with minds opened wide and not a speck of suspicion between them.
translations.idiomatic: The court overlooks faults and forgives past wrongs, winning loyalty through generosity. Men such as Yu Xiaoqing, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, and Ouyang Hui were all taken into the inner circle and given power to act in the emperor's name, with complete trust and not a trace of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 況將軍釁非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮於危亡，何失於富貴！

translations.literal: Moreover, General, your offense is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime differs from Bi Zhen's—why should you worry over ruin, or miss out on wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Your offense, General, is nothing like Zhang Xiu's betrayal, your guilt nothing like Bi Zhen's treachery—why fear destruction, or forfeit wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth point.

sentences.zh: 方今周、齊鄰睦，境外無虞，並兵一向，匪朝伊夕，非劉、項競逐之機，楚、趙連從之勢；

translations.literal: At present Zhou and Qi are friendly neighbors, with no worries beyond the borders; their combined armies will advance in one direction, and it will be a matter of no more than a morning or an evening—not a moment like when Liu and Xiang contended, nor a situation like when Chu and Zhao joined in alliance;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Qi are on friendly terms now, with no threat on the frontiers. Their armies will march together, and not a day will pass before they arrive—not a season for Liu Bang and Xiang Yu to contend, nor a chance for Chu and Zhao to league together as of old;

sentences.zh: 何得雍容高拱，坐論西伯哉！

translations.literal: how can you sit at ease with hands folded high, discoursing like the Earl of the West?
translations.idiomatic: how can you sit at ease with folded hands, playing the philosopher-king of the west?

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth point.

sentences.zh: 且留將軍狼顧一隅，亟經摧衄，聲實虧喪，膽氣衰沮。

translations.literal: Moreover, General, you have glanced back like a wolf from your corner, repeatedly suffering defeats; your reputation and substance are diminished, your courage and spirit decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, General, you have held your corner with a wolf's wary glance, suffering defeat after defeat until your name and strength are spent and your courage broken.

sentences.zh: 其將帥首鼠兩端，唯利是視，孰能被堅執銳，長驅深入，繫馬埋輪，奮不顧命，以先士卒者乎！

translations.literal: Your generals and commanders are like a rat at either end of a beam, looking only to profit—who among them could don hard armor, grasp sharp weapons, drive deep in a long advance, tie their horses and bury their wheels, and rush forward heedless of death to lead the troops?
translations.idiomatic: Your officers waver between two sides, caring only for gain—who among them would don armor, take up sharp weapons, drive deep into enemy country, stake horses and bury wheels, and charge ahead without regard for his life to lead the men?

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sixth point.

sentences.zh: 將軍之強，孰如侯景？

translations.literal: Was the General's strength ever equal to Hou Jing's?
translations.idiomatic: Was your power ever equal to Hou Jing's?

sentences.zh: 將軍之眾，孰如王琳？

translations.literal: Were the General's hosts ever equal to Wang Lin's?
translations.idiomatic: Were your troops ever equal to Wang Lin's?

sentences.zh: 武皇滅侯景於前，今上摧王琳於後，此乃天時，非復人力。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu destroyed Hou Jing before, and the present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after—this was the season ordained by Heaven, no longer a matter of human effort alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu destroyed Hou Jing; the present emperor crushed Wang Lin. That was Heaven's timing, not human strength alone.

sentences.zh: 且兵革已後，民皆厭亂，其孰能棄墳墓，捐妻子，出萬死不顧水計，從將軍於白刃之間乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, after years of arms and armor the people are weary of disorder—who could abandon their ancestral graves, cast aside wife and children, and face ten thousand deaths without counting the cost, to follow the General between flashing blades?
translations.idiomatic: After so many years of war the people are sick of chaos—who would leave his ancestors' graves, abandon wife and children, and march into certain death to follow you between crossed swords?

sentences.zh: 七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the seventh point.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前古，子陽、季孟，傾覆相尋；

translations.literal: Looking back through antiquity, Ziyang and Jimeng met ruin in succession;
translations.idiomatic: Look to the past: Ziyang and Jimeng fell one after another;

sentences.zh: 餘善、右渠，危亡繼及。

translations.literal: Yushan and Youqu, peril and extinction followed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yushan and Youqu brought disaster upon themselves in turn.

sentences.zh: 天命可畏，山川難恃。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate is to be feared; mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate inspires awe; mountains and rivers are poor defenses.

sentences.zh: 況將軍欲以數郡之地當天下之兵，以諸侯之資拒天子之命，強弱逆順，可得侔乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, General, you wish to pit the territory of a few commanderies against the armies of the empire, and oppose the Son of Heaven's command with the resources of a regional lord—can strength and weakness, right and wrong, be made equal?
translations.idiomatic: And you would hold a few commanderies against the armies of the realm, and set a regional lord's means against the Son of Heaven's command—can such a mismatch ever be evened?

sentences.zh: 八也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the eighth point.

sentences.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異；

translations.literal: Moreover, those not of our kindred by nature have hearts that must differ;
translations.idiomatic: Those who are not of our kin will not have our hearts;

sentences.zh: 不愛其親，豈能及物！

translations.literal: if one does not love his own kin, how can he reach others?
translations.idiomatic: a man who does not love his own kin cannot be trusted to care for others.

sentences.zh: 留將軍身縻國爵，子尚王姬，猶且棄天屬而弗顧，背明君而孤立，危亡之日，豈能同憂共患，不背將軍者乎！

translations.literal: General Liu holds a state enfeoffment in his own person, and his son is married to an imperial princess—yet he still abandons Heaven's kin without regard and turns his back on the enlightened ruler to stand alone. On the day of peril and ruin, can he share worry and disaster with you, and not turn against you?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi holds a state fief and his son is married to an imperial princess—yet he has already cast aside his own kin and turned from the enlightened sovereign to stand apart. When ruin comes, will he share your fate, or will he not betray you?

sentences.zh: 至於師老力屈，懼誅利賞，必有韓、智晉陽之謀，張、陳井陘之勢。

translations.literal: As for troops grown weary and strength exhausted, fearing punishment and coveting rewards, there will surely arise schemes like Han and Zhi at Jinyang, or situations like Zhang and Chen at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: When your army is exhausted and your strength spent, with men fearing punishment and hungry for reward, you will see plots like Han and Zhi at Jinyang and splits like Zhang Er and Chen Yu at Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 九也。

translations.literal: This is the ninth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the ninth point.

sentences.zh: 北軍萬里遠鬥，鋒不可當。

translations.literal: The northern army fights from ten thousand li away, and its edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: The northern armies have marched a thousand miles to fight, and their spearhead cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 將軍自戰其地，人多顧後；

translations.literal: The General fights on his own ground, and many men look to the rear;
translations.idiomatic: You fight on your own soil, and your men will look homeward;

sentences.zh: 眾寡不敵，將帥不侔。

translations.literal: few cannot match many, and commanders cannot match commanders.
translations.idiomatic: few cannot match many, nor your generals theirs.

sentences.zh: 師以無名而出，事以無機而動，以此稱兵，未知其利。

translations.literal: An army that marches forth without a righteous name, an enterprise moved without opportune timing—raising arms on this basis, one cannot know its advantage.
translations.idiomatic: An army raised without just cause, a campaign launched without opportunity—take up arms on such terms, and I see no profit in it.

sentences.zh: 十也。

translations.literal: This is the tenth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the tenth point.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計，莫若絕親留氏。

translations.literal: For the General's planning, nothing is better than to break ties with the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: For your own sake, General, nothing would be wiser than to sever your bond with the Liu family.

sentences.zh: 遣子入質，釋甲偃兵，一遵詔旨。

translations.literal: Send your son as hostage, lay aside armor and halt weapons, and follow the imperial edict in all things.
translations.idiomatic: Send your son to court as hostage, lay down arms, and obey the throne's commands to the letter.

sentences.zh: 方今籓維尚少，皇子幼沖，凡預宗枝，皆蒙寵樹。

translations.literal: At present the imperial princes are still few, the crown prince young, and all who share in the imperial clan are showered with favor and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan is still thin, the heir young, and every branch of the house is showered with favor and rank.

sentences.zh: 況以將軍之地，將軍之才，將軍之名，將軍之勢，而克修籓服，北面稱臣，寧與劉澤同年而語其功業哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, with the General's territory, the General's talent, the General's name, and the General's power, if you can fulfill your duties as a vassal, face north and call yourself subject—would your achievements not be spoken of in the same breath as Liu Ze's, rather than Liu Yi's?
translations.idiomatic: With your lands, your talent, your name, and your power, if you fulfilled your duties as a loyal vassal and bowed north as a subject, would your achievements not rank with Liu Ze's rather than Liu Yi's?

sentences.zh: 寄感恩懷服，不覺狂言，斧鉞之誅，其甘如薺。」

translations.literal: Ji, moved by gratitude and loyal submission, spoke rash words unaware; execution by axe and halberd would be as sweet as shepherd's purse to me."
translations.idiomatic: Overcome by gratitude and loyalty, I have spoken rashly without thinking; if the axe falls on me, I shall accept it as gladly as a meal of greens."

sentences.zh: 寶應覽書大怒。

translations.literal: When Baoying read the letter he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying read the letter he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 或謂寶應曰：「虞公病勢漸篤，言多錯謬。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Baoying: "Sir Yu's illness is growing severe, and his words are often confused and mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Baoying: "Sir Yu's illness is worsening, and his words are often confused."

sentences.zh: 寶應意乃小釋，亦以寄民望，故優容之。

translations.literal: Baoying's anger then eased somewhat; moreover, because Ji enjoyed the people's esteem, he treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying's anger eased a little, and because Ji enjoyed popular esteem, he treated him leniently.

sentences.zh: 周梁躁公侯莫陳崇從周主如原州。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao of Liang in Zhou, Houmochen Chong, accompanied the Zhou ruler to Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Chong, Duke Zhao of Liang in Northern Zhou, accompanied the Zhou emperor to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝夜還長安，人竊怪其故，崇謂所親曰：「吾此聞術者言，晉公今年不利，車駕今忽夜還，不過晉公死耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor returned to Chang'an by night, and people privately wondered at the reason. Chong said to those close to him: "I have heard the diviners say that the Duke of Jin will have an ill year this year. The imperial carriage has suddenly returned by night—nothing more than that the Duke of Jin will die."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to Chang'an by night, and people whispered about the reason. Chong told his intimates: "I have heard the diviners say the Duke of Jin faces a bad year. The emperor's sudden return tonight can only mean the Duke of Jin is about to die."

sentences.zh: 或發其事。

translations.literal: Someone reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported what he had said.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝召諸公於大德殿，面責崇，崇惶恐謝罪。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the emperor summoned the nobles to the Hall of Great Virtue and rebuked Chong to his face; Chong fearfully begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou the emperor summoned the princes to the Hall of Great Virtue and rebuked Chong to his face. Chong prostrated himself in terror and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 其夜，塚宰護遣使將兵就崇第，逼令自殺，葬如常儀。

translations.literal: That same night Grand Minister Protector Hu sent envoys with troops to Chong's residence and compelled him to take his own life; he was buried with the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Grand Minister Protector Yuwen Hu sent troops to Chong's house and forced him to kill himself. He was buried with the usual honors.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以高州刺史黃法□為南徐州刺史，臨川太守周敷為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On renchen, Huang Fa[?] of Gaozhou was made inspector of South Xuzhou, and Linchuan Administrator Zhou Fu was made inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen, Huang Fatan, inspector of Gaozhou, was appointed inspector of South Xuzhou, and Zhou Fu, administrator of Linchuan, was appointed inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 周主命司憲大夫拓跋迪造《大律》十五篇。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler ordered Director of Law Tuoba Di to compose fifteen chapters of the "Great Code."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor ordered Director of Law Tuoba Di to draft fifteen chapters of the Great Code.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚子，頒行之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengzi, it was promulgated and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day gengzi, the code was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 其制罪：一曰杖刑，自十五至五十；

translations.literal: Its punishments were established as follows: first, beating with the staff, from fifteen to fifty strokes;
translations.idiomatic: The penalties were defined as follows: first, beating with the staff, from fifteen to fifty strokes;

sentences.zh: 二曰鞭刑，自六十至百；

translations.literal: second, flogging with the whip, from sixty to one hundred strokes;
translations.idiomatic: second, flogging with the whip, from sixty to one hundred strokes;

sentences.zh: 三曰徒刑，自一年至五年；

translations.literal: third, penal servitude, from one year to five years;
translations.idiomatic: third, penal servitude, from one to five years;

sentences.zh: 四曰流刑，自二千五百里至四千五百里；

translations.literal: fourth, banishment, from two thousand five hundred li to four thousand five hundred li;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, exile, from two thousand five hundred to four thousand five hundred li;

sentences.zh: 五曰死刑，罄、絞、斬、梟、裂；

translations.literal: fifth, death penalty—strangulation until death, hanging, decapitation, exposure of the head, and dismemberment;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, capital punishment—strangulation, hanging, decapitation, exposure of the head, and dismemberment;

sentences.zh: 凡二十五等。

translations.literal: twenty-five grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-five grades in all.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以司空、南徐州刺史侯安都為江州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Minister of Works and South Xuzhou Inspector Hou Andu was made inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Hou Andu, Minister of Works and inspector of South Xuzhou, was appointed inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，周詔：「大塚宰晉國公，親則懿昆，任當元輔，自今詔誥及百司文書，並不得稱公名。」

translations.literal: On xinyou, Zhou issued an edict: "The Grand Minister Protector, Duke of Jin, is kin of honored closeness and bears the foremost ministerial charge. From this day forward, edicts and all documents of the hundred offices must not use the Duke's personal name."
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou Northern Zhou issued an edict: "The Grand Minister Protector, Duke of Jin, is a close kinsman of the throne and the chief minister of state. Henceforth no edict or document from any office shall use the Duke's personal name."

sentences.zh: 護抗表固讓。

translations.literal: Hu submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu submitted a memorial firmly declining the honor.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day yichou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the month (yichou), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 齊詔司空斛律光督步騎二萬，築勳常城於軹關；

translations.literal: Qi ordered Minister of Works Hulu Guang to supervise twenty thousand infantry and cavalry in building Xunchang Fort at Zhi Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Qi ordered Minister of Works Hulu Guang to direct twenty thousand foot and horse in building Xunchang Fort at Zhi Pass;

sentences.zh: 仍築長城二百里，置十二戍。

translations.literal: and also to build two hundred li of the Long Wall, establishing twelve garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: and to build two hundred li of the Long Wall with twelve garrisons along it.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，齊以兼尚書右僕射趙彥深為左僕射。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Qi made concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu Qi appointed Zhao Yanshen, concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未，周以柱國達奚武為太保。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, Zhou made Pillar of State Daxi Wu Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yiwei, Northern Zhou appointed Daxi Wu, Pillar of State, as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 周主將視學，以太傅燕國公於謹為三老。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler was about to inspect the Imperial Academy and appointed Grand Tutor Yu Jin, Duke of Yan, as one of the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor was about to visit the Imperial Academy and appointed Yu Jin, Grand Tutor and Duke of Yan, as one of the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 謹上表固辭，不許，仍賜以延年杖。

translations.literal: Jin submitted a memorial firmly declining, but this was not permitted; he was moreover granted a staff for prolonging life.
translations.idiomatic: Jin submitted a memorial declining the honor, but the emperor refused and also bestowed on him a staff of longevity.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝幸太學。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the emperor visited the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu the emperor went in person to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 謹入門，帝迎拜於門屏之間，謹答拜。

translations.literal: When Jin entered the gate, the emperor came forward to bow between the gate and the screen; Jin returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin entered the gate, the emperor came forward to bow to him between the gate and the screen, and Jin bowed in return.

sentences.zh: 有司設三老席於中楹，南面。

translations.literal: The officials set the Three Elders' seat at the central pillar, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The officials set the Three Elders' seat at the central pillar, facing south.

sentences.zh: 太師護升階，設幾。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Hu ascended the steps and set out the armrest.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu ascended the steps and set out the armrest table.

sentences.zh: 謹升席，南面憑幾而坐。

translations.literal: Jin ascended to the seat, faced south, and sat leaning on the armrest.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took his seat, faced south, and sat leaning on the armrest.

sentences.zh: 大司馬豆盧寧升階，正舄。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Doulu Ning ascended the steps and straightened his shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Doulu Ning ascended the steps and straightened his shoes.

sentences.zh: 帝升階，立於斧扆之前，西面。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the steps and stood before the axe-and-screen, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the steps and stood before the axe-and-screen symbol of authority, facing west.

sentences.zh: 有司進饌，帝跪設醬豆，親為之袒割。

translations.literal: The officials brought in the feast; the emperor knelt to set out the sauces and beans, and personally bared his shoulder to cut the meat.
translations.idiomatic: The officials brought in the feast. The emperor knelt to set out the sauces and condiments and personally bared his shoulder to carve the meat.

sentences.zh: 謹食畢，帝親跪授爵以酳。

translations.literal: When Jin had finished eating, the emperor knelt in person to present the cup for rinsing the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin had finished eating, the emperor knelt and personally offered the rinsing cup.

sentences.zh: 有司撤訖，帝北面立而訪道。

translations.literal: When the officials had cleared away, the emperor stood facing north and inquired about the Way.
translations.idiomatic: When the dishes were cleared, the emperor stood facing north and asked Jin to instruct him in the Way.

sentences.zh: 謹起，立於席後，對曰：「木受繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: Jin rose and stood behind the seat, replying: "Wood that accepts the line is made straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rose and stood behind his seat, answering: "Wood that accepts the carpenter's line is made straight; a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 明王虛心納諫以知得失，天下乃安。」

translations.literal: An enlightened king with an open mind accepts remonstrance to know gain and loss, and all under Heaven is thereby secure."
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened sovereign who listens with an open mind to know his errors will keep the realm at peace."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「去食去兵，信不可去；

translations.literal: He also said: "One may forgo food and forgo arms, but trust cannot be forgoed;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "A state may lack food or arms, but it cannot lack trust;

sentences.zh: 願陛下守信勿失。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will keep trust and not lose it."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to keep faith and never let it slip."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「有功必賞，有罪必罰，則為善者日進，為惡者日止。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Merit must be rewarded and guilt must be punished; then those who do good advance day by day, and those who do evil cease day by day."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Reward merit and punish wrongdoing without fail, and the virtuous will advance daily while the wicked will hold back."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「言行者，立身之基，願陛下三思而言，九慮而行，勿使有過。

translations.literal: He also said: "Words and conduct are the foundation of establishing the person; I pray Your Majesty will think thrice before speaking and consider nine times before acting, and do not let there be faults.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Speech and action are the pillars of one's standing. May Your Majesty think thrice before you speak and weigh your steps ninefold before you act, so that you never stumble.

sentences.zh: 天子之過，如日月之食，人莫不知，願陛下慎之。」

translations.literal: A Son of Heaven's faults are like eclipses of the sun and moon—no one fails to know them; I pray Your Majesty will be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: The errors of a ruler are like solar or lunar eclipses: everyone sees them. I beg Your Majesty to be ever watchful."

sentences.zh: 帝再拜受言，謹答拜。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice to receive the words; Jin returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice to receive this counsel, and Jin bowed in reply.

sentences.zh: 禮成而出。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he went out.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 司空侯安都恃功驕橫，數聚文武之士騎射賦詩，齋中賓客，動至千人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Hou Andu relied on his achievements and was arrogant and overbearing; he repeatedly gathered civil and military men for mounted archery and composing verse, and guests in his studio often reached a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Hou Andu, bloated by his merits, grew arrogant and domineering. He constantly gathered scholars and soldiers for mounted archery and poetry, and the guests at his residence often numbered a thousand.

sentences.zh: 部下將帥，多不遵法度，檢問收攝，輒奔歸安都。

translations.literal: The generals under his command for the most part did not observe regulations; when investigated and seized, they would at once flee back to Andu.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate commanders routinely flouted the law, and whenever investigators tried to arrest them, they fled straight back to Andu's protection.

sentences.zh: 上性嚴整，內銜之，安都弗之覺。

translations.literal: The emperor was strict and orderly by nature and harbored resentment inwardly; Andu did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stern by temperament and nursed a growing grievance, but Andu never noticed.

sentences.zh: 每有表啟，封訖，有事未盡，開封自書之云：「又啟某事。」

translations.literal: Whenever he had a memorial, after sealing it, if something remained unsaid, he would break the seal and write himself, saying, "Further memorial regarding such-and-such."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he submitted a memorial, if something still weighed on his mind after the seal was applied, he would break it open and add in his own hand, "A further memorial on such-and-such a matter."

sentences.zh: 及侍宴，酒酣，或箕踞傾倚。

translations.literal: When attending banquets, once the wine was deep, he would sometimes sit with legs spread or lean and sprawl.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts, once the wine took hold, he would sprawl with legs apart or slump against the furnishings.

sentences.zh: 嘗陪樂遊園禊飲，謂上曰：「何如作臨川王時？」

translations.literal: Once, while accompanying a spring purification feast at Leye Garden, he said to the emperor, "How does this compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Once at a spring purification banquet in Leye Garden, he asked the emperor, "How does this compare with your days as Prince of Linchuan?"

sentences.zh: 上不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 安都再三言之。

translations.literal: Andu spoke of it again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Andu pressed the question repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此雖天命，抑亦明公之力。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Though this was Heaven's mandate, it was also owing to Your Grace's power."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally replied, "Though Heaven ordained it, it was also your doing, my lord."

sentences.zh: 宴訖，啟借供帳水飾，欲載妻妾於御堂宴飲。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he requested to borrow banquet tents and aquatic decorations, intending to bring his wives and concubines to feast in the imperial hall.
translations.idiomatic: After the feast he asked to borrow the imperial banquet pavilions and aquatic ornaments so he could bring his wives and concubines to dine in the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 上雖許之，意甚不懌。

translations.literal: Although the emperor granted it, in his heart he was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented, but inwardly he was furious.

sentences.zh: 明日，安都坐於御座，賓客居群臣位，稱觴上壽。

translations.literal: The next day Andu sat upon the imperial seat, his guests occupying the ministers' places, raising cups to offer longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Andu took the imperial seat while his guests sat in the ministers' ranks and raised their cups to toast the emperor's long life.

sentences.zh: 會重雲殿災，安都帥將士帶甲入殿，上甚惡之，陰為之備。

translations.literal: When Chongyun Hall caught fire, Andu led armored soldiers into the hall; the emperor greatly detested this and secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyun Hall burned, Andu marched armored troops into the palace. The emperor loathed this show of force and quietly began to prepare against him.

sentences.zh: 及周迪反，朝議謂當使安都討之，而上更使吳明徹。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di rebelled, court opinion held that Andu ought to be sent to suppress him, but the emperor instead sent Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di rose in rebellion, the court expected Hou Andu to be sent against him, but the emperor dispatched Wu Mingche instead.

sentences.zh: 又數遣台使按問安都部下，檢括亡叛。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly sent imperial envoys to investigate Andu's subordinates and search out deserters and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent imperial commissioners again and again to probe Andu's followers and hunt down deserters.

sentences.zh: 安都遣其別駕周弘實自托於舍人蔡景歷，並問省中事。

translations.literal: Andu sent his registrar Zhou Hongshi to entrust himself to Gentleman-of-the-Household Cai Jingli and also to inquire about affairs within the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Andu sent his registrar Zhou Hongshi to win over Gentleman-of-the-Household Cai Jingli and to sound him out on inner-court affairs.

sentences.zh: 景歷錄其狀，具奏之，因希旨稱安都謀反。

translations.literal: Jingli recorded the circumstances, reported them fully, and to please the emperor's intent declared that Andu was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingli recorded every detail, reported it in full, and—reading the emperor's mood—declared that Andu was plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 上慮其不受召，故用為江州。

translations.literal: The emperor feared he would not obey a summons, and therefore appointed him to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Andu would refuse a summons, the emperor posted him as governor of Jiangzhou to draw him away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，安都自京口還建康，部伍入於石頭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Andu returned from Jingkou to Jiankang, and his troops entered Stone Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Andu returned from Jingkou to Jiankang and quartered his troops in Stone Fortress.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝引安都宴於嘉德殿，又集其部下將帥會於尚書朝堂，於坐收安都，囚於嘉德西省，又收其將帥，盡奪馬仗而釋之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor invited Andu to feast at Jiade Hall and also gathered his subordinate generals to meet at the Shangshu morning court; at the seat he seized Andu and imprisoned him in the Jiade western quarters, and also seized his generals, stripped them of all horses and weapons, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor entertained Andu at Jiade Hall, then summoned his commanders to the Masters of Writing assembly hall. There he seized Andu at table and locked him in the western quarters of Jiade Palace. His officers were also taken, stripped of horses and arms, and then released.

sentences.zh: 因出蔡景歷表，以示於朝，乃下詔暴其罪惡，明日，賜死，宥其妻子，資給其喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he produced Cai Jingli's memorial and showed it to the court, then issued an edict exposing his crimes; the next day he granted death, pardoned his wife and children, and provided funds for his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced Cai Jingli's memorial for the court to see and issued an edict listing Andu's crimes. The next day Andu was ordered to take his own life. His wife and children were spared, and the state paid for his burial.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖在京口，嘗與諸將宴，杜僧明、周文育、侯安都為壽，各稱功伐。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu was at Jingkou, he once feasted with the generals; Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu offered toasts for his longevity, each boasting of his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when Gaozu was still at Jingkou, he once feasted with his generals. Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu toasted his health, each boasting of his exploits.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿等悉良將也，而並有所短。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "You are all fine generals, yet each has shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You are all able commanders, but each of you has a fatal flaw.

sentences.zh: 杜公志大而識暗，狎於下而驕於上；

translations.literal: Duke Du is ambitious in will yet dim in judgment, familiar with those below yet arrogant toward those above;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Du aims high but sees poorly—too familiar with his men, too proud toward his superiors;

sentences.zh: 周侯交不擇人，而推心過差；

translations.literal: Marquis Zhou is heedless in choosing associates, yet excessive in giving his heart;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhou befriends anyone without discrimination and gives his trust too freely;

sentences.zh: 侯郎傲誕而無厭，輕佻而肆志；

translations.literal: Lord Hou is arrogant and unrestrained without satiety, frivolous and wilful in spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Hou is insolent, unbounded, and never satisfied—frivolous and reckless in his desires;

sentences.zh: 並非全身之道。」

translations.literal: none of these are ways to preserve the whole person."
translations.idiomatic: none of these are ways to keep oneself alive."

sentences.zh: 卒皆如其言。

translations.literal: In the end all proved as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, every word of it came true.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，齊主使兼散騎常侍崔子武來聘。

translations.literal: On yimao the ruler of Qi sent Concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant Cui Ziwu on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, the Northern Qi ruler dispatched Concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant Cui Ziwu as envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 齊侍中、開府儀同三司和士開有寵於齊主，齊主外朝視事，或在內宴賞，須臾之間，不得不與士開相見，或累日不歸，一日數入；

translations.literal: Qi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Bearer of the Equal in Honor of the First Rank He Shikai had the favor of the Qi ruler; whether the Qi ruler was holding court outside or feasting within, in the space of a moment he could not avoid seeing Shikai, or he might not return for many days and enter several times in one day;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Attendant-in-Ordinary He Shikai, who also held the rank of Bearer of the Equal in Honor of the First Rank, was the darling of the Qi emperor. Whether the ruler was holding court or feasting in the inner palace, he could not go a moment without summoning Shikai. Sometimes he stayed away for days on end, yet entered the inner quarters several times in a single day;

sentences.zh: 或放還之後，俄頃即追，未至之間，連騎督趣，奸諂百端，寵愛日降，前後賞賜，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: or after releasing him to return, within moments he would be pursued; before he had arrived, riders in succession urged him on; flattery and sycophancy in a hundred forms; favor and love poured down day by day; rewards before and after could not be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: and even after dismissing him to go home, he would recall him almost at once, dispatching riders in relays to hurry him back. Shikai flattered him by every art, and the emperor's affection and gifts grew daily beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 每侍左右，言辭容止，極諸鄙褻；

translations.literal: Whenever he attended at the ruler's side, his words, bearing, and deportment were utterly vulgar and obscene;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended the emperor, his speech and manners plumbed the depths of vulgarity;

sentences.zh: 以夜繼晝，無復君臣之禮。

translations.literal: night following upon day, no longer any propriety between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: and day ran into night without a trace of the etiquette owed between sovereign and subject.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂帝曰：「自古帝王，盡為灰土，堯舜、桀紂，竟復何異！

translations.literal: He once said to the emperor, "Since ancient times all emperors and kings end as dust and ashes—Yao and Shun, Jie and Zhou, in the end what difference is there!
translations.idiomatic: He once told the emperor, "Every ruler since antiquity ends as dust. What difference does it make whether one is Yao or Shun, Jie or Zhou?

sentences.zh: 陛下宜及少壯，極意為樂，縱橫行之，一日取快，可敵千年。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought, while still young and strong, to indulge to the utmost in pleasure, carrying it out as you will; one day's taking of joy can match a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should seize your youth and revel without restraint. A single day of pleasure is worth a thousand years of care.

sentences.zh: 國事盡付大臣，何慮不辦，無為自勤約也！」

translations.literal: State affairs entirely entrusted to great ministers—why worry that they will not be handled? Do not be frugal and restrained yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Leave state affairs to your ministers—they will manage. Why torment yourself with thrift and discipline?"

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 於是委趙彥深掌官爵，元文遙掌財用，唐邕掌外、騎兵，信都馮子琮、胡長粲常東宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entrusted Zhao Yanshen with offices and titles, Yuan Wenyao with finances, Tang Yong with outer and cavalry armies, and Xindu Feng Ziqiong and Hu Changcan regularly with the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Zhao Yanshen in charge of offices and titles, Yuan Wenyao over finances, Tang Yong over the outer and cavalry forces, and kept Feng Ziqiong of Xindu and Hu Changcan constantly at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝三四日一視朝，書數字而已，略無所言，須臾罷入。

translations.literal: The emperor held court once every three or four days, wrote a few characters only, said virtually nothing, and withdrew shortly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court only once every three or four days, wrote a few characters, said almost nothing, and withdrew within moments.

sentences.zh: 長粲，僧敬之子也。

translations.literal: Changcan was the son of Seng Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Changcan was the son of Hu Sengjing.

sentences.zh: 帝使士開與胡後握槊，河南康獻王孝瑜諫曰：「皇后天下之母，豈可與臣下接手！」

translations.literal: The emperor had Shikai and Empress Hu play liubo; the Prince of Henan, Posthumous name Kangxian, Xiaoyu, remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother of all under Heaven—how can she clasp hands with a subject!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had He Shikai and Empress Hu play liubo together. Prince Xiaoyu of Henan, posthumous name Kangxian, remonstrated: "The empress is mother of the realm. How can she touch hands with a subject!"

sentences.zh: 孝瑜又言：「趙郡王睿，其父死於非命，不可親近。」

translations.literal: Xiaoyu also said, "Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui—his father died an unnatural death; he must not be approached."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu added, "Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery's father died by violence. He must not be trusted."

sentences.zh: 由是睿及士開共譖之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rui and Shikai together slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Rui and Shikai joined in slandering him.

sentences.zh: 士開言孝瑜奢僭，睿言「山東唯聞有河南王，不聞有陛下。」

translations.literal: Shikai said Xiaoyu was extravagant and presumptuous; Rui said, "In Shandong they only hear of the Prince of Henan, not of Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Shikai accused Xiaoyu of extravagance and overstepping his rank, while Rui said, "In the east they know only the Prince of Henan, not Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝由是忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby came to be wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the emperor grew suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 孝瑜竊與爾朱御女言，帝聞之，大怒。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu secretly spoke with the Erzhu imperial woman; when the emperor heard of it, he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that Xiaoyu had been speaking privately with the Erzhu lady of the inner palace, he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 庚申，頓飲孝瑜酒三十七杯。

translations.literal: On gengshen he compelled Xiaoyu to drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen he forced Xiaoyu to down thirty-seven cups of wine in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 孝瑜體肥大，腰帶十圍，帝使左右婁子彥載以出，鴆之於車。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu had a large and corpulent body, his belt ten spans; the emperor had his attendants Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu was enormously fat—his belt ten spans around—and the emperor had his attendants load him into a cart under Lou Ziyan and poison him on the way out.

sentences.zh: 至西華門，煩躁投水而絕。

translations.literal: When he reached Xihua Gate, in agitation he threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Xihua Gate, writhing in torment, he threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 諸侯在宮中者，莫敢舉聲，唯河間王孝琬大哭而出。

translations.literal: Among the princes within the palace, none dared raise a sound; only the Prince of Hejian, Xiaowan, wailed loudly as he went out.
translations.idiomatic: The princes in the palace dared not utter a sound. Only Prince Xiaowan of Hejian burst out wailing as he left.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊辰，周主幸原州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen the Zhou ruler visited Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, on the day wuchen the Northern Zhou emperor visited Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑，齊以三台宮為大興聖寺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, Qi made the Santaigong Palace into the Daxingsheng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day xinchou, Northern Qi converted the Santaigong Palace into the Daxingsheng Temple.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，廣州刺史陽山穆公歐陽頠卒，詔其子紇襲父爵位。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renxu, Guangzhou Governor, Duke of Yangshan with posthumous name Mu, Ouyang Yi died; an edict ordered his son He to inherit his father's title and position.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day renxu, Ouyang Yi, Duke of Yangshan with posthumous name Mu and governor of Guangzhou, died. An edict named his son He to succeed to his father's title and post.

sentences.zh: 甲子，周主自原州登隴。

translations.literal: On jiazi the Zhou ruler from Yuanzhou ascended Long.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi the Zhou emperor crossed from Yuanzhou onto the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 周迪復越東興嶺為寇，辛未，詔護軍章昭達將兵討之。

translations.literal: Zhou Di again crossed Dongxing Ridge as a bandit; on xinwei an edict ordered Guardian of the Army Zhang Zhaoda to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di again raided across Dongxing Ridge. On the day xinwei an edict ordered Guardian of the Army Zhang Zhaoda to take the field against him.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，周主如同州。

translations.literal: On bingxu the Zhou ruler went to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu the Zhou emperor proceeded to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，周人欲與突厥木桿可汗連兵伐齊，許納其女為後，遣御伯大夫楊薦及左武伯大原王慶往結之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Zhou people wished to join arms with the Türk Mughan Khan to attack Qi, promising to take his daughter as empress; they sent Palace Grandee Yang Jian and Left Martial Baron Wang Qing of Taiyuan to cement the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Northern Zhou had sought a joint campaign with the Türk Mughan Khan against Qi, promising his daughter as empress, and sent Palace Grandee Yang Jian and Left Martial Baron Wang Qing of Taiyuan to seal the pact.

sentences.zh: 齊人聞之懼，亦遣使求昏於突厥，賂遺甚厚。

translations.literal: When the Qi people heard of it they were afraid, and also sent envoys to seek marriage with the Türks, their bribes and gifts very rich.
translations.idiomatic: Qi heard of this and panicked, sending its own envoys to seek a marriage alliance with the Türks and lavishing gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 木桿貪齊幣重，欲執薦等送齊。

translations.literal: Mughan, greedy for Qi's gifts because they were heavy, wished to seize Jian and the others and hand them over to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Mughan, coveting Qi's heavier bribes, planned to seize Yang Jian and his party and deliver them to Qi.

sentences.zh: 薦知之，責木桿曰：「太祖昔與可汗共敦鄰好，蠕蠕部落數千來降。

translations.literal: Jian learned of it and reproached Mughan, saying, "The Grand Ancestor once with the Khan deeply honored neighborly relations; Rouran tribes in their thousands came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jian learned of the plot and rebuked Mughan: "The Grand Ancestor once cherished neighborly ties with your khanate. When thousands of Rouran tribesmen came over to us,

sentences.zh: 太祖悉以付可汗使者，以快可汗之意。

translations.literal: the Grand Ancestor entirely handed them to the Khan's envoys to satisfy the Khan's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: he handed them all to your envoys to please your khan.

sentences.zh: 如何今日遽欲背恩忘義，獨不愧鬼神乎？」

translations.literal: How today do you suddenly wish to betray grace and forget righteousness—are you alone not ashamed before the spirits?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you now turn your back on that kindness? Are you not ashamed before Heaven and earth?"

sentences.zh: 木桿慘然良久曰：「君言是也。

translations.literal: Mughan, grim-faced, after a long while said, "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Mughan sat silent a long while, then said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 吾意決矣，當相與共平東賊，然後送女。」

translations.literal: My mind is decided: we shall together pacify the eastern bandits, and then send the girl."
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up. We shall join you in crushing the eastern foe, and only then send the bride."

sentences.zh: 薦等覆命。

translations.literal: Jian and the others returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian and his party returned to report success.

sentences.zh: 公卿請發十萬人擊齊，柱國楊忠獨以為得萬騎足矣。

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers requested sending a hundred thousand men to attack Qi; Pillar-of-State Yang Zhong alone held that ten thousand horsemen would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: The court urged dispatching a hundred thousand men against Qi, but Pillar-of-State Yang Zhong alone argued that ten thousand cavalry would be enough.

sentences.zh: 戊子，遣忠將步騎一萬，與突厥自北道伐齊，又遣大將軍達奚武帥步騎三萬，自南道出平陽，期會於晉陽。

translations.literal: On wuzi he sent Zhong to lead ten thousand infantry and cavalry with the Türks by the northern route to attack Qi, and also sent Grand General Daxi Wu to command thirty thousand infantry and cavalry by the southern route out from Pingyang, with a rendezvous set at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi he sent Yang Zhong with ten thousand foot and horse to invade Qi alongside the Türks by the northern route, and Grand General Daxi Wu with thirty thousand by the southern route through Pingyang, both columns to meet at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，辛酉，章昭達大破周迪。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on xinyou, Zhang Zhaoda greatly defeated Zhou Di.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the eleventh month, on the day xinyou, Zhang Zhaoda routed Zhou Di.

sentences.zh: 迪脫身潛竄山谷，民相與匿之，雖加誅戮，無肯言者。

translations.literal: Di slipped away and hid in the mountains and valleys; the people together concealed him, and though executions were imposed, none would speak.
translations.idiomatic: Di escaped into the hills. The local people hid him, and even under threat of execution none would betray him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛卯，周主還長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 丙申，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingshen there was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 章昭達進軍度嶺，趣建安，討陳寶應，詔益州刺史余孝頃督會稽、東陽、臨海、永嘉諸軍自東道會之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhaoda advanced his army across the ridge toward Jian'an to attack Chen Baoying; an edict ordered Yizhou Governor Yu Xiaoling to supervise the armies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia from the eastern route to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda marched over the ridge toward Jian'an to subdue Chen Baoying. An edict ordered Yu Xiaoling, governor of Yizhou, to command the forces of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia along the eastern route to link up with him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，初祭始興昭烈王於建康，用天子禮。

translations.literal: That year, for the first time they sacrificed to Prince Zhaolie of Shixing at Jiankang, using the rites of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chen performed for the first time in Jiankang the imperial rites of sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 周楊忠拔齊二十餘城。

translations.literal: Zhou's Yang Zhong captured more than twenty Qi cities.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Yang Zhong took more than twenty Qi cities.

sentences.zh: 齊人守陘嶺之隘，忠擊破之。

translations.literal: The Qi men guarded the narrow pass at Yinling; Zhong broke through them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi troops held the Yinling pass, but Yang Zhong broke through.

sentences.zh: 突厥木桿、地頭、步離三可汗以十萬騎會之。

translations.literal: The Türk khans Mughan, Titou, and Buli with a hundred thousand horsemen joined him.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk khans Mughan, Titou, and Buli joined him with a hundred thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 己丑，自恆州三道俱入。

translations.literal: On jichou from Hengzhou all three routes entered together.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou all three columns advanced from Hengzhou at once.

sentences.zh: 時大雪數旬，南北千餘里，平地數尺。

translations.literal: At the time great snow fell for many tens of days; for more than a thousand li north and south the level ground was several chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell for weeks on end, blanketing more than a thousand li north to south to a depth of several feet on the open plain.

sentences.zh: 齊主自鄴倍道赴之，戊午，至晉陽。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler from Ye marched by double stages to the scene; on wuwu he reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor rushed from Ye by forced marches and on the day wuwu reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 斛律光將步騎三萬屯平陽。

translations.literal: Hulü Guang led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry and encamped at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Guang camped at Pingyang with thirty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 己未，周師及突厥逼晉陽。

translations.literal: On jiwei the Zhou army and the Türks pressed upon Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei the Zhou army and the Türks closed on Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 齊主畏其強，戎服率宮人東走，欲避之。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler feared their strength, donned military dress, and led palace women east in flight, intending to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified by their strength, the Qi emperor donned armor and fled east with his palace women to escape them.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王睿、河間王孝琬叩馬諫。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and Prince of Hejian Xiaowan knocked on his horse to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and Prince Xiaowan of Hejian seized his horse's bridle and pleaded with him to stay.

sentences.zh: 孝琬請委睿部分，必得嚴整。

translations.literal: Xiaowan requested that Rui's division be entrusted to him, and that strict order would surely be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan urged the emperor to place Rui's troops under his command, promising that he could restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，命六軍進止皆取睿節度，而使并州刺史段韶總之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented, ordering that the advance and halt of the six armies all follow Rui's command, while making Bingzhou Governor Duan Shao overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, placing all six armies under Rui's tactical command while appointing Duan Shao, governor of Bingzhou, as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚申朔，齊主登北城，軍容甚整。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengshen the new moon, the Qi ruler ascended the north wall; the army's appearance was very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, the day gengshen, the Qi emperor mounted the north wall of Jinyang. His troops stood in impeccable order.

sentences.zh: 突厥咎周人曰：「爾言齊亂，故來伐之。

translations.literal: The Türks reproached the Zhou men, saying, "You said Qi was in disorder, and therefore came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks reproached the Zhou envoys: "You told us Qi was in chaos, and that is why we came to fight.

sentences.zh: 今齊人眼中亦有鐵，何可當耶！」

translations.literal: Now the Qi men's eyes also have iron—how can they be withstood!"
translations.idiomatic: Now we see iron in the eyes of the Qi soldiers. Who could stand against them!"

sentences.zh: 周人以步卒為前鋒，從西山下去城二里許。

translations.literal: The Zhou men took infantry as vanguard, descending from the west mountain to within about two li of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army sent its infantry forward, descending the western hills to within about two li of the walls.

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹欲逆擊之，段韶曰：「步卒力勢，自當有限。

translations.literal: All the generals wished to strike them in counterattack; Duan Shao said, "Infantry in strength and momentum is by nature limited.
translations.idiomatic: Every commander wanted to counterattack, but Duan Shao said, "Foot soldiers can only push so hard.

sentences.zh: 今積雪既厚，逆戰非便，不如陳以待之。

translations.literal: Now the accumulated snow is already deep; fighting against them is not advantageous—better to array and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: The snow is deep, and a meeting engagement would be awkward. Better to hold our formation and let them come.

sentences.zh: 彼勞我逸，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: They labor while we rest; breaking them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: They will be weary and we fresh. We are sure to crush them."

sentences.zh: 既至，齊悉其銳兵鼓噪而出。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Qi mustered all its elite troops, beating drums and shouting as they went out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou vanguard arrived, Qi threw its finest troops into the field with thunderous drums and war cries.

sentences.zh: 突厥震駭，引上西山，不肯戰，周師大敗而還。

translations.literal: The Türks were struck with terror, drew up onto West Mountain, refused to fight, and the Zhou army was utterly defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the Türks retreated up West Mountain and refused to give battle. The Zhou army was routed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 突厥引兵出塞，縱兵大掠，自晉陽以往七百餘里，人畜無遺。

translations.literal: The Türks led their troops out of the passes and let their soldiers plunder on a vast scale; for more than seven hundred li from Jinyang onward, neither man nor beast was left.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks withdrew beyond the frontier and unleashed wholesale pillage. For seven hundred li and more west of Jinyang, they left no person or animal alive.

sentences.zh: 段韶追之，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Duan Shao pursued them but did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao gave chase but dared not close with them.

sentences.zh: 突厥還至陘嶺，凍滑，乃輔氈以度。

translations.literal: When the Türks returned to Xing Ridge, the ice was frozen slippery; they then spread felt to cross.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Xing Ridge the ice was treacherous with frost, so they laid felt to cross it.

sentences.zh: 胡馬寒瘦，膝已下皆無毛，比至長城，馬死且盡，截槊杖之以歸。

translations.literal: The barbarians' horses, chilled and emaciated, had no hair below the knee; by the time they reached the Great Wall the horses were nearly all dead—they cut off spear shafts and used them as walking sticks to return.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses, wasted by cold, were hairless to the knee. By the time they reached the Great Wall nearly all the horses were dead; they cut spear-shafts for staffs and limped home.

sentences.zh: 達奚武至平陽，未知忠退。

translations.literal: Daxi Wu reached Pingyang, not yet knowing that Yang Zhong had withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu marched to Pingyang, unaware that Yang Zhong had already pulled back.

sentences.zh: 斛律光與書曰：「鴻鵠已翔於寥廓，羅者猶視於沮澤。」

translations.literal: Hulü Guang wrote to him: "The swan goose has already soared into the vast sky, yet the fowler still gazes at the marshy pool."
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Guang sent him a letter: "The wild swan has already risen into the open sky, yet the fowler still watches the bog."

sentences.zh: 武得書，亦還。

translations.literal: Wu received the letter and also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu received the letter, he too withdrew.

sentences.zh: 光逐之，入周境，獲二千餘口而還。

translations.literal: Guang pursued him, entered Zhou territory, captured more than two thousand captives, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guang pursued him into Zhou territory, took more than two thousand captives, and returned.

sentences.zh: 光見帝於晉陽，帝以新遭大寇，抱光頭而哭。

translations.literal: Guang appeared before the emperor at Jinyang; the emperor, having just suffered a great incursion, embraced Guang's head and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang came before the emperor at Jinyang, the emperor—fresh from a devastating raid—clasped Guang's head and wept.

sentences.zh: 任城王湝進曰：「何至於此！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Rencheng, Hui, stepped forward and said, "How can it go so far as this!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rencheng Hui advanced and said, "Surely it need not come to this!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With that the emperor ceased.

sentences.zh: 初，齊顯祖之世，周人常懼齊兵西度，每至冬月，守河椎冰。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the era of the Qi Founding Emperor, the Zhou men constantly feared that Qi troops would cross westward; every winter month they guarded the river and rammed the ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Wenxuan of Qi, the Zhou constantly feared a Qi thrust across the river. Every winter they posted guards to break up the ice.

sentences.zh: 及世祖即位，嬖倖用事，朝政漸紊，齊人椎冰以備周兵之逼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wucheng took the throne, favorites monopolized affairs, court government grew increasingly chaotic, and the Qi men now rammed the ice to guard against the Zhou army's pressure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wucheng came to the throne, minions ran the government and the court fell into disorder; now it was the Qi who broke the ice, lest Zhou armies press upon them.

sentences.zh: 斛律光憂之，曰：「國家常有吞關、隴之志，今日至此，而唯玩聲色乎！」

translations.literal: Hulü Guang was distressed by this and said, "The state has always had the ambition to swallow the passes and Long—you've come to this today, and yet only indulge in sound and beauty!"
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Guang was troubled and said, "Our state has always hungered to seize the passes and Long—yet you have brought us to this pass and only dally with music and women!"

sentences.zh: 辛巳，上祀北郊。

translations.literal: On xinyi, the emperor sacrificed at the Northern Suburban Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyi the emperor offered sacrifice at the Northern Suburban Altar.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengyin the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of gengyin, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 初，齊顯祖命群官刊定魏《麟趾格》為《齊律》，久而不成。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Qi Founding Emperor had ordered the officials to revise and fix the Northern Wei Linzhi Code into the Qi Code; for long it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wenxuan had ordered his officials to adapt the Northern Wei "Linzhi Code" into the Qi statutes, but the work dragged on unfinished.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，決獄罕依律文，相承謂之「變法從事」。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many; in deciding cases they rarely followed the written statutes—in succession this was called "changing the law to get things done."
translations.idiomatic: With endless military and civil crises, judges seldom looked to the written law; by custom they spoke of "changing the law to suit the case."

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，思革其弊，乃督修律令者，至是而成，《律》十二篇，《令》四十卷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wucheng took the throne, he thought to reform this abuse and supervised those revising laws and orders; by now it was completed—twelve fascicles of Statutes, forty scrolls of Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng, wishing to end the abuse, pressed the drafters until at last the code was done: twelve chapters of statutes and forty scrolls of ordinances.

sentences.zh: 其刑名有五：一曰死，重者轘之，次梟首，次斬，次絞；

translations.literal: Its punishments by name were five: first, death—in severity wheel-sundering, next decapitation and display, next beheading, next strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: Five classes of punishment were named: death—severe cases by crushing in a wheel, then exposure of the head, then beheading, then strangulation;

sentences.zh: 二曰流，投邊裔為兵；

translations.literal: second, exile—sent to the border regions as soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: exile—banishment to the frontier as soldiery;

sentences.zh: 三曰刑，自五歲至一歲；

translations.literal: third, penal servitude—from five years down to one year;
translations.idiomatic: forced labor—from five years down to one;

sentences.zh: 四曰鞭，自百至四十；

translations.literal: fourth, flogging—from one hundred down to forty;
translations.idiomatic: flogging—from one hundred strokes down to forty;

sentences.zh: 五曰杖，自三十至十；

translations.literal: fifth, beating with the staff—from thirty down to ten;
translations.idiomatic: beating with the rod—from thirty down to ten;

sentences.zh: 凡十五等。

translations.literal: fifteen grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: fifteen grades in all.

sentences.zh: 其流內官及老、小、閹、癡並過失應贖者，皆以絹代金。

translations.literal: For exile, inner officials, and the old, young, castrated, imbecilic, and those whose faults merited redemption, all used silk in place of money fines.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles, palace officials, the aged, the young, eunuchs, the feeble-minded, and offenders who might redeem their guilt all paid in silk instead of cash.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉，班行之，因大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinyou, it was promulgated and put into effect, and a great amnesty followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinyou, the code was promulgated and a general amnesty declared.

sentences.zh: 是後為吏者始守法令。

translations.literal: After this those who served as officials began for the first time to observe the laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did magistrates begin to govern by the written law.

sentences.zh: 又敕仕門子弟常講習之，故齊人多曉法。

translations.literal: He also ordered that sons of official families regularly practice and study them, so the people of Qi largely came to understand the law.
translations.idiomatic: He further commanded that sons of the official class study the code regularly, so that many in Qi came to know the law.

sentences.zh: 又令民十八受田輸租調，二十充兵，六十免力役，六十六還田，免租調。

translations.literal: He also ordered that at eighteen the people should receive fields and pay land tax and household levies, at twenty enter military service, at sixty be exempt from corvée labor, at sixty-six return fields and be exempt from land tax and household levies.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed: at eighteen one received land and paid rent and levies; at twenty one entered military service; at sixty one was freed from corvée; at sixty-six one surrendered the land and was exempt from rent and levies.

sentences.zh: 一夫受露田八十畝，婦人四十畝，奴婢依良人，牛受六十畝。

translations.literal: One adult male received eighty mu of dew-field; a woman forty mu; slaves and maidservants followed freemen; an ox received sixty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Each adult male took eighty mu of open-field; a woman forty; slaves and servants followed the quota for commoners; an ox sixty.

sentences.zh: 大率一夫一婦調絹一匹，綿八兩，墾租二石，義租五斗；

translations.literal: As a rule one man and one woman paid household levy of one bolt of silk, eight ounces of cotton, field rent two dan, charity rent five dou;
translations.idiomatic: As a rule a household of one man and one woman paid one bolt of silk in levy, eight ounces of cotton, two dan of field rent, and five dou of charity grain;

sentences.zh: 奴婢准良人之半；

translations.literal: slaves and maidservants at half the freeman rate;
translations.idiomatic: slaves and servants at half that rate;

sentences.zh: 牛調二尺，墾租一鬥，義租五升。

translations.literal: an ox: levy two chi of silk, field rent one dou, charity rent five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: an ox: two chi of silk in levy, one dou of field rent, five sheng of charity grain.

sentences.zh: 墾租送台，義租送郡以備水旱。

translations.literal: Field rent was sent to the central government; charity rent was sent to the commandery to prepare for flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Field rent went to the capital; charity grain to the commandery as a reserve against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 己巳，齊群盜田子禮等數十人，共劫太師彭城景思王浟為主，詐稱使者，逕向浟第，至內室，稱敕，牽浟上馬，臨以白刃，欲引向南殿，浟大呼不從，盜殺之。

translations.literal: On jisi, several dozen bandits of Qi such as Tian Zili and others together seized the Grand Preceptor, Prince of Pengcheng Jingsi, Wang You, as their leader, falsely claiming to be envoys, went straight to You's residence, entered the inner chamber, proclaimed an edict, pulled You onto a horse, held white blades to him, wished to lead him to the Southern Hall—You shouted and would not obey, and the bandits killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi several dozen Qi bandits led by Tian Zili seized the Grand Preceptor, Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng, Wang You, as their figurehead. Posing as imperial envoys, they went straight to You's mansion, entered the inner quarters, proclaimed an edict, and forced him onto a horse at sword-point, intending to march him to the Southern Hall. You cried out and refused; the robbers killed him.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，周初令百官執笏。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Zhou for the first time ordered the hundred officials to hold hu tablets.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Zhou first required all officials to carry court tablets.

sentences.zh: 齊以斛律光為司徒，武興王普為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Qi made Hulü Guang Minister over the Masses and Prince of Wuxing Pu Director of the Left Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi appointed Hulü Guang Minister over the Masses and Prince Wuxing Pu Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 普，歸彥之兄子也。

translations.literal: Pu was the nephew of Guiyan's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a nephew of Guiyan on his elder brother's side.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以馮翊王潤為司空。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Prince of Fengyi Run was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Prince Fengyi Run was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，齊主使兼散騎常侍皇甫亮來聘。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao, the Qi ruler sent Concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Huangfu Liang on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao the Qi emperor sent the concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Huangfu Liang on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 庚子，周主遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Zhou ruler sent envoys on a mission of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Zhou emperor sent envoys in return.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，周以鄧公河南竇熾為大宗伯。

translations.literal: On guimao, Zhou made Duke of Deng, Henan Dou Chi, Grand lineage master.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zhou appointed Duke of Deng, Dou Chi of Henan, Grand Master of Lineage.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，封世宗之子賢為畢公。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, enfeoffed heir apparent's son Xian as Duke of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renxu, they enfeoffed the heir apparent's son Xian as Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 甲子，齊主還鄴。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Qi ruler returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Qi emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 壬午，齊以趙郡王睿為錄尚書事，前司徒婁睿為太尉。

translations.literal: On renwu, Qi made Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui recorder of the Masters of Writing, former Minister over the Masses Lou Rui Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Qi made Prince Zhao Rui Recorder of the Masters of Writing and the former Minister over the Masses Lou Rui Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以段韶為太師。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Duan Shao was made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Duan Shao was made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以任城王湝為大將軍。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Prince of Rencheng Hui was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Prince Rencheng Hui was made Grand General.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Qi ruler went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 周以太保達奚武為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhou made Grand Tutor Daxi Wu governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou appointed Grand Tutor Daxi Wu governor of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 六月，齊主殺樂陵王百年。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Qi ruler killed Prince of Leling Wang Bainen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Qi emperor executed Prince Leling, Wang Bainen.

sentences.zh: 時白虹圍日再重，又橫貫而不達，赤星見，齊主欲以百年厭之。

translations.literal: At that time a white rainbow encircled the sun in two folds, and again crossed horizontally without reaching through; a red star appeared—the Qi ruler wished to use Bainen to appease it.
translations.idiomatic: A double white halo ringed the sun, and a horizontal streak cut across without closing; a red star appeared. The emperor meant to offer up Bainen to appease Heaven.

sentences.zh: 會博陵人賈德冑教百年書，百年嘗作數敕字，德冑封以奏之。

translations.literal: It happened that Jia Dezhou of Boling taught Bainen writing; Bainen once wrote several characters of an imperial edict, and Dezhou sealed it and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dezhou of Boling had been teaching Bainen to write. Bainen once copied several characters of an edict; Dezhou sealed the sheet and reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝發怒，使召百年。

translations.literal: The emperor flew into rage and sent to summon Bainen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and summoned Bainen.

sentences.zh: 百年自知不免，割帶□夬留與其妃斛律氏，見帝於涼風堂。

translations.literal: Bainen knew himself beyond escape, cut his belt and jade ring and left them for his consort, the Lady Hulü, and appeared before the emperor in the Cool Wind Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Bainen cut his belt and jade ring and left them for his consort, Lady Hulü, then presented himself in the Cool Wind Hall.

sentences.zh: 使百年書敕字，驗與德冑所奏相似，遣左右亂捶之，又令曳之繞堂行且捶，所過血皆遍地，氣息將盡，乃斬之，棄諸池，池水盡赤。

translations.literal: He had Bainen write the edict characters; verified against what Dezhou had submitted—it was similar. He sent attendants to beat him at random, and again had him dragged around the hall while beating; wherever they passed the blood covered the ground. His breath was nearly gone—then he was beheaded and cast into a pool, and the pool water turned entirely red.
translations.idiomatic: He made Bainen write the edict characters; the hand matched Dezhou's report. Attendants beat him at will, then dragged him around the hall, striking as they went until the floor ran with blood. When he was nearly dead they beheaded him and threw the body into a pool until the water was all red.

sentences.zh: 妃把□夬哀號不食，月餘亦卒，□夬猶在手，拳不可開；

translations.literal: The consort took the jade ring and wailed, refusing food; after more than a month she also died—the jade ring was still in her hand, her fist could not be opened;
translations.idiomatic: The consort clutched the jade ring, wailed, and refused food; after more than a month she died too, the ring still in her fist, which would not open;

sentences.zh: 其父光自擘之，乃開。

translations.literal: her father Guang tore it apart himself, and only then did it open.
