translations.idiomatic: her father Guang pried the fingers apart himself before it would yield.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，周改御伯為納言。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Zhou changed Director of Attendants to Intendant of Speech.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Zhou renamed the Director of Attendants the Intendant of Speech.

sentences.zh: 初，周太祖之從賀拔岳在關中也，遣人迎晉公護於晉陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhou Taizu followed Heba Yue in Guanzhong, he sent men to welcome Duke of Jin Hu from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder Yuwen Tai followed Heba Yue in the Guanzhong region, he sent men to bring Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 護母閻氏及周主之姑皆留晉陽，齊人以配中山宮。

translations.literal: Hu's mother Lady Yan and the Zhou ruler's paternal aunt were both left at Jinyang; the Qi men assigned them to the Zhongshan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's mother Lady Yan and the Zhou emperor's aunt were left behind in Jinyang and assigned by Qi to the Zhongshan Palace.

sentences.zh: 及護用事，遣間使入齊求之，莫知音息。

translations.literal: When Hu came to power, he sent secret envoys into Qi to seek them, but no word could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hu held power he sent secret agents into Qi to find them, but heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊遣使者至玉壁，求通互市。

translations.literal: Qi sent envoys to Yubi seeking to open mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent envoys to Yubi to propose border trade.

sentences.zh: 護欲訪求母、姑，使司馬下大夫尹公正至玉壁，與之言，使者甚悅。

translations.literal: Hu wished to inquire after his mother and aunt; he sent Acting Secretariat Lower Grand Master Yin Gongzheng to Yubi to speak with them—the envoys were very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hu wished to learn news of his mother and aunt and sent Acting Lower Grand Master of the Secretariat Yin Gongzheng to Yubi to parley; the Qi envoys were delighted.

sentences.zh: 勳州刺史韋孝寬獲關東人，復縱之，因致書為言西朝欲通好之意。

translations.literal: Xun Province Governor Wei Xiaokuan captured men from east of the Pass, released them again, and through them sent a letter stating that the Western court wished to communicate good intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Province governor Wei Xiaokuan captured easterners, then released them with a letter expressing the Western court's wish for peace.

sentences.zh: 是時，周人以前攻晉陽不得志，謀與突厥再伐齊。

translations.literal: At this time, because the Zhou men's earlier attack on Jinyang had not achieved their aim, they plotted with the Türks to attack Qi again.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou, frustrated in their earlier assault on Jinyang, now plotted with the Türks for a second invasion of Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊主聞之，大懼，許遣護母西歸，且求通好，先遣其姑歸。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler heard of it and was greatly afraid; he agreed to send Hu's mother west and moreover sought good relations, first sending his aunt back.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor was terrified, agreed to send Hu's mother west, and sued for peace, returning the aunt first.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丁亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on dinghai the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the new moon of dinghai, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 周遣柱國楊忠將兵，會突厥伐齊，至北河而還。

translations.literal: Zhou sent Pillar of State Yang Zhong with troops to join the Türks in attacking Qi; they reached the North River and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent the pillar of state Yang Zhong with an army to join the Türks against Qi; they reached the North River and turned back.

sentences.zh: 戊子，周以齊公憲為雍州牧，宇文貴為大司徒。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Zhou made Duke of Qi Xian governor of Yong Province, Yuwen Gui Grand Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Zhou made Duke Qi Xian governor of Yong Province and Yuwen Gui Grand Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁巳，以衛公直為大司馬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Duke of Wei Zhi was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Duke Wei Zhi was made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 追錄佐命元功，封開府儀同三司隴西公李昺為唐公，太馭中大夫長樂公若干鳳為徐公。

translations.literal: Posthumously recording meritorious supporters at the founding, enfeoffed Defender of the Palace with credentials equal to the Three Ducal Ministers of Longxi, Li Bing, as Duke of Tang; Grand Driver of the Center, Duke of Changle, Qianyu Feng, as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious founders were honored posthumously: Li Bing of Longxi, Defender of the Palace with credentials equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, was enfeoffed Duke of Tang; Qianyu Feng of Changle, Grand Driver of the Center, was enfeoffed Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 昺，虎之子；

translations.literal: Bing was the son of Hu the Tiger;
translations.idiomatic: Bing was the son of Li Hu the Tiger;

sentences.zh: 鳳，惠之子也。

translations.literal: Feng was the son of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was the son of Qianyu Hui.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，齊主封其子綽為南陽王，儼為東平王。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Qi ruler enfeoffed his son Chuo as Prince of Nanyang, Yan as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Qi emperor enfeoffed his sons Chuo as Prince of Nanyang and Yan as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 儼，太子之母弟也。

translations.literal: Yan was the younger brother of the crown prince on the mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the crown prince's younger uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇齊幽州，眾十餘萬，入長城，大掠而還。

translations.literal: The Türks raided You Province of Qi—more than a hundred thousand men—they entered the Great Wall, plundered greatly, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand Türks raided Qi's You Province, broke through the Great Wall, plundered heavily, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 周皇姑之歸也，齊主遣人為晉公護母作書，言護幼時數事，又寄其所著錦袍，以為信驗。

translations.literal: When the Zhou emperor's paternal aunt returned, the Qi ruler had someone compose a letter for Duke of Jin Hu's mother, relating several incidents from Hu's childhood, and also sent the brocade robe she had made as proof of authenticity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor's aunt returned west, the Qi court drafted a letter for Duke of Jin Hu's mother, recalling episodes from his boyhood, and sent the brocade robe she had woven as proof.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「吾屬千載之運，逢大齊之德，矜老開恩，許得相見。

translations.literal: And it said: "We belong to a fortune of a thousand years, and meet the great virtue of Great Qi—pitying the old and opening grace, permission was granted to meet.
translations.idiomatic: It read: "By a thousand-year fate we have met the great kindness of Great Qi; in pity for an old woman grace was opened and reunion permitted.

sentences.zh: 禽善草木，母子相依。

translations.literal: Birds cherish grass and trees; mother and child depend on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Birds and beasts cherish their thickets; mother and child lean on one another.

sentences.zh: 吾有可罪，與汝分離！

translations.literal: I had fault enough to be separated from you!
translations.idiomatic: I had sins enough to be torn from you!

sentences.zh: 今復何福，還望見汝！

translations.literal: What blessing is it now, that I may again hope to see you!
translations.idiomatic: What fortune is left that I may yet look on your face!

sentences.zh: 言此悲喜，死而更蘇。

translations.literal: Speaking this—both grief and joy—as if dead and then revived.
translations.idiomatic: To speak these words is both sorrow and joy, as though one died and woke again.

sentences.zh: 世間所有，求皆可得，母子異國，何處可求！

translations.literal: Everything in the world, sought, can all be obtained—mother and son in different states, where can it be sought!
translations.idiomatic: All that the world holds may be sought and found—yet mother and son in rival realms, where shall we seek each other?

sentences.zh: 假汝貴極王公，富過山海，有一老母，八十之年，飄然千里，死亡旦夕，不得一朝暫見，不得一日同處，寒不得汝衣，饑不得汝食。

translations.literal: Suppose you were noble to the utmost of kings and dukes, wealth surpassing mountains and seas—yet there is one old mother, eighty years old, drifting a thousand li, death morning or evening, unable to see you even for one morning, unable to dwell together even for one day—cold and cannot obtain your garment, hungry and cannot obtain your food.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose you rose to the highest rank, wealth vaster than mountains and seas—still there is one old mother, eighty years old, adrift a thousand li, death at any dawn, unable to see you for a single morning or share a single day: in cold she has not your coat; in hunger she has not your food.

sentences.zh: 汝雖窮榮極盛，光耀世間，於吾何益！

translations.literal: Though you reached the limit of glory and splendor, shining across the world—what use is it to me!
translations.idiomatic: Though you shine with glory across the world, what good is it to me?

sentences.zh: 吾今日之前，汝既不得申其供養，事往何論；

translations.literal: Before today you could not extend your support—I forbear to speak of what is past;
translations.idiomatic: Before today you could not care for me—let the past go;

sentences.zh: 今日以後，吾之殘命，唯繫於汝爾。

translations.literal: after today my remaining life hangs only on you.
translations.idiomatic: from today my frail life hangs on you alone.

sentences.zh: 戴天履地，中有鬼神，勿雲冥昧，而可欺負！」

translations.literal: Bearing heaven on one's head and treading earth underfoot—among them are ghosts and spirits; do not say it is dark and obscure, and can be deceived!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven above and earth below hold spirits; do not think the unseen may be cheated!"

sentences.zh: 護得書，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Hu received the letter and could not master his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Hu read the letter and was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 復書曰：「區宇分崩，遭遇災禍，違離膝下，三十五年。

translations.literal: He wrote in reply: "The realm was split apart, I met with disaster, parted from beneath your knees thirty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The realm shattered; disaster struck; for thirty-five years I have been far from your knee.

sentences.zh: 受形稟氣，皆知母子，誰同薩保，如此不教！

translations.literal: Receiving form and receiving breath—all know mother and son—who is like the sabao, so lacking in teaching!
translations.idiomatic: All who draw breath know mother and child—who but a Sogdian chief would fail to teach his own?

sentences.zh: 子為公侯，母為俘隸，暑不見母暑，寒不見母寒，衣不知有無，食不知饑飽，泯如天地之外，無由暫聞。

translations.literal: The son is duke and marquis, the mother is captive and slave—in heat I do not see mother's heat, in cold I do not see mother's cold—clothes unaware whether they exist, food unaware of hunger or fullness—lost as beyond heaven and earth, with no means of even briefly hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I am duke and marquis while you are captive and slave; in summer I cannot know your summer, in winter your winter; I know neither whether you have clothes nor whether you eat—lost beyond heaven and earth, with no word from you.

sentences.zh: 分懷冤酷，終此一生，死若有知，冀奉見於泉下耳！

translations.literal: Separately cherishing cruel injustice, to end this one life—if the dead have awareness, I hope only to attend and see you in the springs below!
translations.idiomatic: I nurse this cruel wrong to the end of my days; if the dead have knowing, I pray only to serve you in the shades.

sentences.zh: 不謂齊朝解網，惠以德音，磨敦、四姑，並話矜放。

translations.literal: I did not expect the Qi court to loosen the net, graciously with words of virtue—Modun and the Fourth Aunt were both said to be shown compassionate release.
translations.idiomatic: I never thought Qi would loosen the net and speak mercy—Modun and Fourth Aunt were both said to be freed.

sentences.zh: 初聞此旨，魂爽飛霸佔，號天叩地，不能自勝。

translations.literal: When I first heard this edict, my spirit soared and flew—I cried to heaven and beat the ground, unable to master myself.
translations.idiomatic: At the first word my soul seemed to fly; I cried to heaven and struck the earth, beyond restraint.

sentences.zh: 齊朝霈然之恩，既已沾洽，有家有國，信義為本，伏度來期，已應有日。

translations.literal: The Qi court's expansive grace has already saturated and spread—with family and with state, trust and righteousness are the foundation; I bow and judge that the day of return ought already to be near.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's sweeping grace has already touched us; for home and realm, faith is the root. I bow and trust the day of your return cannot be far.

sentences.zh: 一得奉見慈顏，永畢生願。

translations.literal: Once able to attend and see your kindly countenance, my life's wish would be forever fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: To see your face even once would fulfill my dearest wish in life.

sentences.zh: 生死肉骨，豈過今恩；

translations.literal: To give flesh to the dead and bone to the living—how could any favor surpass today's grace;
translations.idiomatic: To restore the dead to flesh and the living to bone—no kindness could exceed this;

sentences.zh: 負山載岳，未足勝荷。」

translations.literal: Bearing mountains and carrying peaks would not suffice to bear the load."
translations.idiomatic: Bearing mountains and carrying ridges would still fall short of what I owe."

sentences.zh: 齊人留護母，使更與護書，邀護重報，往返再三。

translations.literal: The men of Qi detained Hu's mother and made her write again to Hu, inviting Hu to send a weighty reply, back and forth several times.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held Hu's mother and had her write to him again and again, pressing him for fuller replies until the exchange had gone back and forth many times.

sentences.zh: 時段韶拒突厥軍於塞下，齊主遣黃門徐世榮乘傳繼周書問韶。

translations.literal: At this time Duan Shao was repelling the Tujue army below the frontier passes; the ruler of Qi sent Yellow Gate Attendant Xu Shirong to ride the post relay and follow up on Zhou's letters to ask Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao was then holding the Turks at bay on the frontier, and the Qi ruler sent Attendant Xu Shirong post-haste with Zhou's letters to ask Shao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 韶以「周人反覆，本無信義，比晉陽之役，其事可知。

translations.literal: Shao said, "The men of Zhou are changeable and deceitful, fundamentally lacking trust and righteousness—as with the campaign at Jinyang, the matter can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied, "The Zhou are treacherous and faithless by nature; the Jin-yang campaign showed what they are capable of.

sentences.zh: 護外托為相，其實主也。

translations.literal: Hu outwardly pretends to be chancellor, but in truth he is the master.
translations.idiomatic: Hu poses as minister while he is really the power behind the throne.

sentences.zh: 既為母請和，不遣一介之使。

translations.literal: Since he seeks peace for his mother's sake, he does not send even a single envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Though he pleads for peace for his mother's sake, he has not sent a single envoy.

sentences.zh: 若據移書，即送其母，恐示之以弱。

translations.literal: If according to their transferred letter we immediately send his mother, we fear showing them our weakness.
translations.idiomatic: If we return his mother at once on their written demand, we will only show weakness.

sentences.zh: 不如且外許之，待和親堅定，然後遣之未晚。」

translations.literal: It would be better for now outwardly to promise them, wait until the marriage-alliance is firm, and then send her—not too late."
translations.idiomatic: Better to promise them outwardly for now and send her only after the alliance is secure—that will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 齊主不聽，即遣之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Qi would not listen and immediately sent her.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler would not listen and sent her at once.

sentences.zh: 閻氏至周，舉朝稱慶，周主為之大赦。

translations.literal: Lady Yan arrived in Zhou; the whole court proclaimed celebration; the Zhou ruler for her sake proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Yan reached Zhou the whole court rejoiced, and the Zhou emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 凡所資奉，窮極華盛。

translations.literal: Everything provided for her support reached the utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Everything provided for her was as lavish as could be.

sentences.zh: 每四時伏臘，周主帥諸親戚行家人之禮，稱觴上壽。

translations.literal: Every year at the seasonal observances of Fuxi and Layue, the Zhou ruler led all his kin in performing family rites, raising cups and offering longevity wishes.
translations.idiomatic: At each seasonal festival the Zhou ruler led the royal kindred in family rites, raising cups to toast her long life.

sentences.zh: 突厥自幽州還，留屯塞北，更集諸部兵，遣使告周，欲與共擊齊如前約。

translations.literal: The Tujue returned from Youzhou, remained encamped north of the passes, again gathered troops of all their tribes, sent envoys to tell Zhou they wished jointly to strike Qi as in the previous pact.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks withdrew from Youzhou, camped north of the frontier, mustered tribal forces again, and sent envoys to Zhou offering a joint attack on Qi as previously agreed.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙巳，突厥寇齊幽州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on yisi, the Tujue raided Qi's Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the intercalary month the Turks raided Qi's Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉公護新得其母，未欲伐齊；

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu had newly obtained his mother and did not wish to attack Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu had only just recovered his mother and had no wish to attack Qi;

sentences.zh: 又恐負突厥約，更生邊患，不得已，征二十四軍及左右廂散隸秦、隴、巴、蜀之兵並羌、胡內附者，凡二十萬人。

translations.literal: He also feared breaking the pact with the Tujue and bringing fresh border troubles; having no choice, he mobilized the twenty-four armies and the scattered troops of the left and right wings subordinate to Qin, Long, Ba, and Shu, together with Qiang and Hu who had submitted within the borders—in all two hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he feared breaking faith with the Turks and inviting fresh border trouble, so against his will he mobilized the twenty-four armies, the scattered forces of Qin, Long, Ba, and Shu, and submitted Qiang and Hu tribesmen—two hundred thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，周主授護斧鉞於廟庭；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the Zhou ruler invested Hu with axe and battle-axe in the ancestral temple court;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi the Zhou emperor invested Hu with the axe and yue at the ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，親勞軍於沙苑；

translations.literal: On dingmao, he personally encouraged the army at Shayuan;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he personally reviewed the troops at Shayuan;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，還官。

translations.literal: On guiyou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 護軍至潼關，遣柱國尉遲迥帥精兵十萬為前鋒，趣洛陽，大將軍權景宣帥山南之兵趣懸瓠，少師楊檦出軹關。

translations.literal: Hu's army reached Tong Pass; he sent Pillar of State Yuchi Jiong to lead one hundred thousand picked troops as vanguard, pressing toward Luoyang; Grand General Quan Jingxuan to lead the troops south of the mountains toward Xuanhu; Junior Preceptor Yang Biao out through Zhi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu's army reached Tong Pass he sent Pillar of State Yuchi Jiong forward with one hundred thousand elite troops toward Luoyang, Grand General Quan Jingxuan with the southern forces toward Xuanhu, and Junior Preceptor Yang Biao through Zhi Pass.

sentences.zh: 周迪復出東興，宣城太守錢肅鎮東興，以城降迪。

translations.literal: Zhou Di again emerged from Dongxing; Xuancheng Governor Qian Su garrisoned Dongxing and surrendered the city to Di.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di rose again from Dongxing; Xuancheng governor Qian Su, who held Dongxing, surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 吳州刺史陳詳將兵擊之，詳兵大敗，迪眾復振。

translations.literal: Wuzhou Governor Chen Xiang led troops to strike him; Xiang's army was greatly defeated, and Di's host revived its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou governor Chen Xiang attacked him but was routed, and Di's forces rallied anew.

sentences.zh: 南豫州刺史西豐脫侯周敷帥所部擊之，至定川，與迪對壘。

translations.literal: Southern Yuzhou Governor Xifeng Tuohou Zhou Fu led his command to attack him; reaching Dingchuan, he faced Di across the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yuzhou governor Zhou Fu of Xifeng led his troops against him and at Dingchuan pitched camp opposite Di.

sentences.zh: 迪紿敷曰：「吾昔與弟戮力同心，豈規相害！

translations.literal: Di deceived Fu, saying, "In former days you and I strove together with one heart—how could I plan to harm you!
translations.idiomatic: Di deceived Fu, saying, "We once fought side by side with one heart—how could I mean to harm you!

sentences.zh: 今願伏罪還朝，因弟披露心腑，先乞挺身共盟。」

translations.literal: Now I wish to submit my crime and return to court; through you, younger brother, I lay bare my inmost heart—I first beg to bare my person and swear the covenant together."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to surrender and return to court; through you, brother, I would lay bare my heart—let me first step forward and swear the pact with you."

sentences.zh: 敷許之，方登壇，為迪所殺。

translations.literal: Fu assented; just as he was mounting the altar, he was killed by Di.
translations.idiomatic: Fu agreed; but as he mounted the altar Di killed him.

sentences.zh: 陳寶應據建安、晉安二郡，水陸為柵，以拒章昭達。

translations.literal: Chen Baoying held Jian'an and Jin'an commanderies, building palisades by land and water to resist Zhang Zhaoda.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baoying held Jian'an and Jin'an and threw up land and water barriers against Zhang Zhaoda.

sentences.zh: 昭達與戰，不利，因據上流，命軍士伐木為筏，施拍其上。

translations.literal: Zhaoda fought him but it went ill; he therefore seized the upper stream, ordered the soldiers to cut timber for rafts, and fitted battering rams atop them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda met him in battle without success, then took the upstream position and had his men cut timber into rafts fitted with battering rams.

sentences.zh: 會大雨江漲，昭達放筏沖寶應水柵，盡壞之，又出兵攻其步軍。

translations.literal: It happened that great rain swelled the river; Zhaoda released the rafts to ram Baoying's water palisades and destroyed them all, and also sent out troops to attack his infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains swelled the river; Zhaoda sent the rafts downstream to smash Baoying's water barriers and also attacked his infantry.

sentences.zh: 方合戰，上遣將軍余孝頃自海道適至，並力乘之。

translations.literal: Just as battle joined, the emperor sent General Yu Xiaoping, who arrived in time by the sea route, and they joined strength to press the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: As battle was joined the emperor's general Yu Xiaoping arrived by sea in the nick of time, and they pressed the attack together.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己丑，寶應大敗，逃至莆口，謂其子曰：「早從虞公計，不至今日。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jichou, Baoying was greatly defeated, fled to Pukou, and said to his son, "Had we early followed Master Yu's plan, we would not have come to today."
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the eleventh month Baoying was routed and fled to Pukou, telling his son, "Had we heeded Master Yu's counsel sooner, we would not be here today."

sentences.zh: 昭達追擒之，並擒留異及其族黨。

translations.literal: Zhaoda pursued and captured him, and also captured Liu Yi and his clan and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda overtook and seized him, together with Liu Yi and his kin and followers.

sentences.zh: 送建康，斬之。

translations.literal: They were sent to Jiankang and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent to Jiankang and executed.

sentences.zh: 異子貞臣以尚主得免，寶應賓客皆死。

translations.literal: Yi's son Zhenchen, because he had married an imperial princess, was spared; Baoying's retainers all died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Zhenchen was spared because he had married a princess; all of Baoying's clients were put to death.

sentences.zh: 上聞虞寄嘗諫寶應，命昭達禮遣詣建康。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Yu Ji had once remonstrated with Baoying and ordered Zhaoda to send him with courtesy to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yu Ji had once counseled Baoying against rebellion, the emperor ordered Zhaoda to escort him respectfully to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 既見，勞之曰：「管寧無羌？」

translations.literal: Once he had been received, the emperor comforted him, saying, "Has Guan Ning no Qiang?"
translations.idiomatic: When they met the emperor greeted him, saying, "All well with you, Guan Ning?"

sentences.zh: 以為衡陽王掌書記。

translations.literal: He was made secretary to the Prince of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary to the Prince of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 周晉公護進屯弘農。

translations.literal: Zhou's Duke of Jin Hu advanced and encamped at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu advanced and encamped at Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 甲午，尉遲迥洛陽，雍州牧齊公憲、同州刺史達奚武、漢州總管王雄軍於邙山。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Yuchi Jiong reached Luoyang; Yongzhou Governor Duke of Qi Xian, Tongzhou Governor Daxi Wu, and Hanzhou Commander-in-Chief Wang Xiong arrayed their armies on Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Yuchi Jiong reached Luoyang; Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian, Tongzhou governor Daxi Wu, and Hanzhou commander Wang Xiong drew up on Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，齊主使兼散騎常侍劉逖來聘。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the ruler of Qi sent Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Liu Ti as envoy on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the Qi ruler sent Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Liu Ti on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 初，周楊檦為邵州刺史，鎮捍東境二十餘年，數與齊戰，未嘗不捷，由是輕之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou's Yang Biao was Shaozhou Governor, garrisoning and defending the eastern border more than twenty years; he fought Qi many times and never failed to win—thereby he came to look down on them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Biao of Zhou had been Shaozhou governor, holding the eastern frontier for more than twenty years and never losing a fight with Qi, and so he grew contemptuous of them.

sentences.zh: 既出軹關，獨引兵深入，又不設備。

translations.literal: Having passed out through Zhi Pass, he alone led troops deep in, and again made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: After marching out through Zhi Pass he pushed deep alone without taking precautions.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，齊太尉婁睿將兵奄至，大破□剽軍，檦遂降齊。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Qi's Grand Commandant Lou Rui led troops that came upon them suddenly and routed □ Biao's army; Biao then surrendered to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Qi's grand commandant Lou Rui fell on him suddenly and routed Yang Biao's army, and Biao surrendered to Qi.

sentences.zh: 權景宣圍懸瓠，十二月，齊豫州道行台、豫州刺史太原王士良、永州刺史蕭世怡並以城降之。

translations.literal: Quan Jingxuan besieged Xuanhu; in the twelfth month, Qi's Xingtai of Yuzhou Route, Yuzhou Governor Taiyuan Wang Shiliang, and Yongzhou Governor Xiao Shiyi all surrendered their cities to him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingxuan besieged Xuanhu; in the twelfth month Qi's route commander for Yuzhou, Yuzhou governor Wang Shiliang of Taiyuan, and Yongzhou governor Xiao Shiyi all surrendered their cities.

sentences.zh: 景宣使開府郭彥守豫州，謝徹守永州，送士良、世怡及降卒千人於長安。

translations.literal: Jingxuan sent Opening the Mansion Guo Yan to hold Yuzhou, Xie Che to hold Yongzhou, and sent Shiliang, Shiyi, and one thousand surrendered soldiers to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan left Guo Yan to hold Yuzhou and Xie Che Yongzhou, and sent Shiliang, Shiyi, and a thousand surrendered troops to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 周人為土山、地道以攻洛陽，三旬不克。

translations.literal: The men of Zhou built earthen mounds and underground passages to attack Luoyang; in thirty days they did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou raised earthworks and dug tunnels against Luoyang but failed to take it in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 晉公護命諸將塹斷河陽路，遏齊救兵，然後同攻洛陽；

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu ordered the generals to trench and cut the Heyang road, check Qi's relief troops, and then jointly attack Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu ordered his generals to trench and block the Heyang road to stop Qi relief, then attack Luoyang together;

sentences.zh: 諸將以為齊兵必不敢出，唯張斥候而已。

translations.literal: the generals thought Qi troops would surely not dare come out, and only spread scouts—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: but the generals assumed Qi would never dare sally out and only posted scouts.

sentences.zh: 齊遣蘭陵王長恭、大將軍斛律光救洛陽，畏周兵之強，未敢進。

translations.literal: Qi sent Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong and Grand General Hulü Guang to rescue Luoyang; they feared the Zhou army's strength and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Prince Lanling Gao Changgong and grand general Hulü Guang to relieve Luoyang, but they feared the Zhou host and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 齊主召并州刺史段韶，謂曰：「洛陽危急，今欲遣王救之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Qi summoned Bingzhou Governor Duan Shao and said to him, "Luoyang is in peril; now I wish to send you to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler summoned Bingzhou governor Duan Shao and said, "Luoyang is in peril and I mean to send you to save it.

sentences.zh: 突厥在北，復須鎮御，如何？」

translations.literal: The Tujue are in the north, and we must again guard and control them—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are in the north and still need guarding—what then?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「北虜侵邊，事等疥癬。

translations.literal: He replied, "The northern barbarians invade the border—the matter is like scabies.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Northern raids are a mere scab on the skin.

sentences.zh: 今西鄰窺逼，乃腹心之病，請奉詔南行。」

translations.literal: Now the western neighbor spies and presses—it is a disease of the heart and belly; I beg to receive the edict and march south."
translations.idiomatic: The western foe at our vitals is the mortal sickness; I beg leave to march south on your command."

sentences.zh: 齊主曰：「朕意亦爾。」

translations.literal: The ruler of Qi said, "My mind is likewise."
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler said, "My mind is the same."

sentences.zh: 乃令韶督精騎一千發晉陽。

translations.literal: He then ordered Shao to command one thousand picked horsemen and set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Shao to take one thousand elite horsemen from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，齊主亦自晉陽赴洛陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the ruler of Qi also himself went from Jinyang to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Qi ruler himself set out from Jinyang for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 己未，齊太宰平原靖翼王淹卒。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Qi's Grand Mentor, Prince Jingyi of Pingyuan Yan, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Qi's grand mentor, Prince Jingyi of Pingyuan Gao Yan, died.

sentences.zh: 段韶自晉陽，行五日濟河，會連日陰霧，壬戌，韶至洛陽，帥帳下三百騎，與諸將登邙阪，觀周軍形勢。

translations.literal: Duan Shao from Jinyang, traveling five days crossed the river; it happened that for successive days there was overcast mist; on renxu, Shao reached Luoyang, led three hundred horsemen of his personal guard, and with the generals ascended the Mang slope to observe the Zhou army's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao left Jinyang, crossed the river after five days' march through days of fog, and on renxu reached Luoyang; with three hundred household troops and the other commanders he climbed the Mang slopes to survey the Zhou positions.

sentences.zh: 至太和谷，與周軍遇，韶即馳告諸營，追集騎士，結陳以待之。

translations.literal: Reaching Taihe Valley, they met the Zhou army; Shao immediately galloped to inform the camps, gathered pursuing knights, and formed battle array to await them.
translations.idiomatic: At Taihe Valley they met the Zhou army; Shao galloped to the camps, rallied the cavalry, and formed line to receive them.

sentences.zh: 韶為左軍，蘭陵王長恭為中軍，鈄律光為右軍。

translations.literal: Shao was the left army, Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong the center army, and Hulü Guang the right army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao took the left, Prince Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right.

sentences.zh: 周人不意其至，皆恟懼。

translations.literal: The men of Zhou did not expect their arrival and were all alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had not expected them and were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 韶遙謂周人曰：「汝宇文護才得其母，遽來為寇，何也？」

translations.literal: Shao called from afar to the men of Zhou, saying, "You—Yuwen Hu has only just obtained his mother, yet you hasten to come as raiders—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao shouted to the Zhou, "You there—Yuwen Hu has only just got his mother back, yet you hurry here to raid—why?"

sentences.zh: 周人曰：「天遣我來，有何可問！」

translations.literal: The men of Zhou said, "Heaven sent us—what is there to ask!"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou answered, "Heaven sent us—what is there to ask!"

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「天道賞善罰惡，當遣汝送死來耳！」

translations.literal: Shao said, "Heaven's way rewards the good and punishes the evil—it should have sent you to deliver your deaths!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao retorted, "Heaven rewards the good and punishes the wicked—it should have sent you here to die!"

sentences.zh: 周人以步兵在前，上山逆戰。

translations.literal: The men of Zhou had infantry in front, ascending the hill to meet battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou put their infantry in front and climbed the hill to fight.

sentences.zh: 韶且戰且卻以誘之；

translations.literal: Shao fought while withdrawing to lure them;
translations.idiomatic: Shao fought while falling back to lure them on;

sentences.zh: 待其力弊，然後下馬擊之。

translations.literal: when their strength was spent, then he dismounted and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: and when their strength failed he dismounted and counterattacked.

sentences.zh: 周師大敗，一時瓦解，投墜溪谷死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The Zhou army was greatly defeated; in one moment it dissolved; those who cast themselves into streams and ravines and died were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army was shattered at once; multitudes fell into streams and ravines and died.

sentences.zh: 蘭陵王長恭以五百騎突入周軍，遂至金墉城下。

translations.literal: Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong with five hundred horsemen burst into the Zhou army and then reached below the Jinyong walls.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lanling broke into the Zhou lines with five hundred horsemen and reached the walls of Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 城上人弗識，長恭免冑示之面，乃下弩手救之。

translations.literal: The men atop the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show them his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders did not know him until he removed his helmet and showed his face; then they sent crossbowmen down to cover him.

sentences.zh: 周師在城下者亦解圍遁去，委棄營幕，自邙山至穀水，三十里中，軍資器械，彌滿川澤。

translations.literal: The Zhou army below the walls also broke the siege and fled, abandoning camps and curtains; from Mount Mang to the Gu River, within thirty li, military stores and weapons filled streams and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou below the walls also broke off and fled, abandoning camps; for thirty li from Mount Mang to the Gu River arms and supplies choked the streams.

sentences.zh: 唯齊公憲、達奚武及庸忠公王雄在後，勒兵拒戰。

translations.literal: Only Duke of Qi Xian, Daxi Wu, and Duke of Loyalty Wang Xiong were in the rear, urging troops to resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: Only Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian, Daxi Wu, and Loyal Duke Wang Xiong held the rear and tried to fight a rearguard action.

sentences.zh: 王雄馳馬沖斛律光陳，光退走，雄追之。

translations.literal: Wang Xiong galloped his horse and charged Hulü Guang's formation; Guang retreated and fled, and Xiong pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong charged Hulü Guang's line at a gallop; Guang fell back and Xiong pursued.

sentences.zh: 光左右皆散，唯餘一奴一矢。

translations.literal: Guang's attendants all scattered; only one slave and one arrow remained.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's escort scattered until only one servant and one arrow were left.

sentences.zh: 雄按槊不及光者丈餘，謂光曰：「吾惜爾不殺，當生將爾見天子。」

translations.literal: Xiong pressed his lance but could not reach within more than ten feet of Guang; he said to Guang, "I spare you and will not kill you—I shall take you alive to show you to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's lance fell more than ten feet short of Guang; he cried, "I spare you—I mean to take you alive before the emperor."

sentences.zh: 光射雄中額，雄抱馬走，至營而卒。

translations.literal: Guang shot Xiong in the forehead; Xiong embraced his horse and fled, and reached camp but died.
translations.idiomatic: Guang shot him in the forehead; Xiong clung to his horse, reached camp, and died.

sentences.zh: 軍中益懼。

translations.literal: Within the army fear increased yet more.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲拊循督勵，眾心小安。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Xian soothed and encouraged with hand and voice, and the hearts of the host were slightly calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xian rallied and encouraged the men, and morale steadied a little.

sentences.zh: 至夜，收軍，憲欲待明更戰。

translations.literal: By night they gathered the army; Xian wished to wait for dawn and fight again.
translations.idiomatic: At night they regrouped; Xian meant to renew the fight at dawn.

sentences.zh: 達奚武曰：「洛陽軍散，人情震駭，若不因夜速還，明日欲歸不得。

translations.literal: Daxi Wu said, "The Luoyang army is scattered, men's hearts are shaken with terror—if we do not take advantage of night to return swiftly, tomorrow we will wish to return but cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu said, "The Luoyang force is broken and the men are terrified; if we do not withdraw tonight, tomorrow we may not get away at all.

sentences.zh: 武在軍久，備見形勢；

translations.literal: Wu has been in the army long and has fully seen how situations unfold;
translations.idiomatic: I have been long in the field and know how these moments turn;

sentences.zh: 公少年未經事，豈可以數營士卒委之虎口乎！」

translations.literal: you, sir, are young and have not yet passed through affairs—how can you consign several camps of soldiers to a tiger's maw!"
translations.idiomatic: you are young and untested—will you leave thousands of men in the tiger's jaws?"

sentences.zh: 乃還。

translations.literal: They then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew.

sentences.zh: 權景宣亦棄豫州走。

translations.literal: Quan Jingxuan also abandoned Yuzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingxuan also abandoned Yuzhou and fled.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，齊主至洛陽。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the ruler of Qi reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Qi ruler reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以段韶為太宰，斛律光為太尉，蘭陵王長恭為尚書令。

translations.literal: On jisi, he made Duan Shao Grand Mentor, Hulü Guang Grand Commandant, and Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he appointed Duan Shao grand mentor, Hulü Guang grand commandant, and Prince Lanling director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 壬申，齊主如虎牢，遂自滑台如黎陽，丙子，至鄴。

translations.literal: On renshen, the ruler of Qi went to Hulao, then from Huatai toward Liyang; on bingzi, he reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Qi ruler went to Hulao, then from Huatai to Liyang, and on bingzi reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 楊忠引兵出沃野，應接突厥，軍糧不給，諸軍憂之，計無所出。

translations.literal: Yang Zhong led troops out of Woye to link up with the Tujue; army grain was not supplied, the armies were troubled, and no plan could be found.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong marched from Woye to support the Turks, but supplies ran out and the troops despaired with no remedy in sight.

sentences.zh: 忠乃招誘稽胡酋長鹹在坐，詐使河州刺史王傑勒兵鳴鼓而至，曰：「大塚宰已平洛陽，欲與突厥共討稽胡之不服者。」

translations.literal: Zhong then summoned and enticed the Ji Hu tribal chiefs who were all seated, falsely made Hezhou Governor Wang Jie sound drums and arrive with troops, and said, "The Grand Minister of Works has already pacified Luoyang and wishes jointly with the Tujue to punish the Ji Hu who will not submit."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then summoned the Ji Hu chiefs who were present and staged a ruse, having Hezhou governor Wang Jie march in with drums beating, and announced, "The grand minister of works has taken Luoyang and means to join the Turks in punishing disobedient Ji Hu."

sentences.zh: 坐者皆懼，忠慰諭而遣之。

translations.literal: Those seated were all afraid; Zhong comforted and instructed them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs were terrified; Zhong soothed them and sent them off.

sentences.zh: 於是諸胡相帥饋輸，車糧填積。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various Hu led one another in presenting supplies; carts and grain piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribes brought supplies in succession until carts and grain piled high.

sentences.zh: 屬周師罷歸，忠亦還。

translations.literal: It happened that the Zhou army ceased and returned; Zhong also returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army withdrew, Zhong withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 晉公護本無將略，是行也，又非本心，故無功，與諸將稽首謝罪。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu fundamentally lacked military strategy; this campaign moreover was not from his heart—therefore he achieved nothing, and with the generals he bowed his head and apologized for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu had little gift for command and had undertaken the campaign unwillingly, so he gained nothing; he and his generals bowed and asked pardon.

sentences.zh: 周主慰勞罷之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler comforted and encouraged them and dismissed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor comforted them and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊山東大水，饑死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: This year, east of the mountains in Qi there was great flood; those who starved to death were countless.
translations.idiomatic: That year great floods struck eastern Qi and the dead from famine were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁彌定屢寇周邊，周大將軍田弘討滅之，以其地置宕州。

translations.literal: King of Dangchang Liang Miding repeatedly raided Zhou's borders; Zhou's Grand General Tian Hong campaigned, destroyed him, and on his territory established Dangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dangchang king Liang Miding raided the Zhou frontier repeatedly; Zhou grand general Tian Hong destroyed him and established Dangzhou on his lands.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，齊以任城王湝為大司馬。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guimao, Qi made the Prince of Rencheng, Xie, Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, on guimao Northern Qi appointed Prince Xie of Rencheng as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: The ruler of Qi went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor traveled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛丑，周遣陳公純、許公貴、神武公竇毅、南陽公楊薦等備皇后儀衛行殿，並六宮百二十人，詣突厥可汗牙帳逆女。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinchou, Zhou sent the Duke of Chen Chun, the Duke of Xu Gui, the Duke Shenwu Dou Yi, the Duke of Nanyang Yang Jian, and others, equipped with the queen's ceremonial guards, traveling palace, and one hundred twenty persons of the six palaces, to proceed to the Tujue khan's yurt camp to welcome the bride.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinchou, Northern Zhou dispatched Duke Chun of Chen, Duke Gui of Xu, Duke Shenwu Dou Yi, Duke Jian of Nanyang Yang, and others with the empress's full ceremonial escort, a mobile palace, and one hundred twenty women of the inner quarters to the Turk khan's encampment to receive the bride.

sentences.zh: 毅，熾之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the elder brother's son of Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi was a nephew of Dou Chi.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，周以柱國安武公李穆為大司空，綏德公陸通為大司寇。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Zhou made the Pillar of State, Duke Anwu Li Mu, Grand Minister of Works, and the Duke of Suide Lu Tong, Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Zhou appointed pillar of state Duke Anwu Li Mu as Grand Minister of Works and Duke of Suide Lu Tong as Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 壬申，周主如岐州。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Zhou ruler went to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Zhou emperor went to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲寅，以安成王頊為司空。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, he made the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, on jiayin Chen appointed Prince Xu of Ancheng as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 頊以帝弟之重，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Because of Xu's weight as the emperor's younger brother, his power tilted the court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's brother, Xu wielded power that overshadowed the entire court.

sentences.zh: 直兵鮑僧睿，恃頊勢為不法，御史中丞徐陵為奏彈之，從南台官屬引奏案而入。

translations.literal: Straight Troop Bao Senrui, relying on Xu's power, acted unlawfully; Censor-in-Chief Xu Ling drafted a memorial impeaching him and, with Southern Tribunal officials, led the memorial case in to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Straight Troop Bao Senrui abused his position under Xu's patronage; Censor-in-Chief Xu Ling drafted an impeachment and entered with Southern Tribunal staff bearing the memorial case.

sentences.zh: 上見陵章服嚴肅，為斂容正坐。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing Ling's robes and demeanor stern, for his part composed his expression and sat upright.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xu Ling's grave bearing and formal dress, the emperor composed himself and sat upright.

sentences.zh: 陵進讀奏版，時頊在殿上侍立，仰視上，流汗失色，陵遣殿中御史引頊下殿。

translations.literal: Ling advanced and read the memorial board; at that time Xu was attending in the hall standing by, looking up at the emperor, sweating and losing color; Ling sent a palace censor to lead Xu down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling stepped forward and read the memorial aloud; Xu, who had been standing attendance in the hall, looked up at the throne, pale and sweating; Xu Ling had a palace censor escort him from the hall.

sentences.zh: 上為之免頊侍中、中書監，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: The emperor on his account removed Xu from Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat; the court became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Xu of his posts as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat, and the court was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 丙午，齊大將軍東安王婁睿坐事免。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Qi's Grand General, the Prince of Dong'an Lou Rui, because of an affair was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Northern Qi dismissed Grand General Prince Lou Rui of Dong'an for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 齊著作郎祖珽，有文學，多技藝，而疏率無行。

translations.literal: Qi's Gentleman of Composition Zu Ting had literary learning and many skills, yet was careless in manner and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting, Gentleman of Composition in Qi, was learned and skilled in many arts, but coarse and unprincipled.

sentences.zh: 嘗為高祖中外府功曹，因宴失金叵羅，於珽髻上得之；

translations.literal: He once served as a merit officer in the Central and Outer Office under Emperor Gaozu; at a banquet a gold wine bowl was lost and was found on Ting's topknot;
translations.idiomatic: He had once been a clerk in the central and outer office under Gao Huan; at a banquet a gold wine bowl went missing and was found tucked in Ting's hair;

sentences.zh: 又坐詐盜官粟三千石，鞭二百，配甲坊。

translations.literal: again he was convicted of fraudulently stealing three thousand piculs of official grain, was flogged two hundred strokes, and assigned to the armorer's workshop.
translations.idiomatic: he was later convicted of embezzling three thousand piculs of government grain, flogged two hundred strokes, and sent to the armorer's workshop.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，珽為秘書丞，盜《華林遍略》，及有它贓，當絞，除名為民。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzu, Ting was Secretary Deputy Director; he stole the 《Compendium of the Flourishing Grove》 and had other stolen goods—he should have been strangled, and his name was struck off to make him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu he served as deputy director of the secretariat, stole the 《Compendium of the Flourishing Grove》, and committed other thefts; though liable to strangulation, he was merely struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 顯祖雖憎其數犯法，而愛其才伎，令直中書省。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Xianzu detested his repeated violations of law, he loved his talents and skills and ordered him to serve directly in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu despised his repeated crimes yet prized his talents and kept him on direct duty in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖為長廣王，珽為胡桃油獻之，因言「殿下有非常骨法。

translations.literal: When Shizu was Prince of Changguang, Ting presented walnut oil to him and thereupon said, "Your Highness has an extraordinary bone pattern.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu was still Prince of Changguang, Ting offered him walnut oil and said, "Your Highness bears the bone structure of an extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 孝征夢殿下乘龍上天。」

translations.literal: Xiaozheng dreamed that Your Highness rode a dragon up to heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozheng dreamed that Your Highness rode a dragon into the sky."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「若然，當使兄大富貴。」

translations.literal: The prince said, "If it is so, you ought to make your elder brother greatly wealthy and noble."
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "If that is so, you ought to make your elder brother rich and honored."

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢拜中書侍郎，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he was promoted and appointed Palace Secretariat Gentleman, then transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince took the throne, Ting was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and then to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 與和士開共為奸諂。

translations.literal: Together with He Shikai he practiced treachery and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: He and He Shikai practiced deceit and flattery together.

sentences.zh: 珽私說士開曰：「君之寵幸，振古無比。

translations.literal: Ting privately spoke to Shikai, saying, "Your favor and grace are without parallel since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Ting told Shikai in private, "Your favor is unmatched in all history.

sentences.zh: 宮車一日晚駕，欲何以克終？」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage one day sets out late, how will you bring matters to a secure end?"
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage departs one day, how will you secure your future?"

sentences.zh: 士開因從問計。

translations.literal: Shikai thereupon followed and asked for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai then asked him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 珽曰：「宜說主上云：『文襄、文宣、孝昭之子，俱不得立，今宜令皇太子早踐大位，以定君臣之分。』

translations.literal: Ting said, "You ought to persuade the sovereign, saying, 'The sons of Wenxiang, Wenxuan, and Xiaozhao were all unable to be established; now it is fitting to have the crown prince early tread the great position, to fix the distinction between ruler and minister.'
translations.idiomatic: Ting said, "You should tell the emperor: 'The sons of Wenxiang, Wenxuan, and Xiaozhao were none of them enthroned; the crown prince should now ascend early to fix the order between ruler and subject.'

sentences.zh: 若事成，中宮、少主必皆德君，此萬全之計也。

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds, the empress and the young sovereign will surely all owe you virtue—this is a plan of ten thousandfold security.
translations.idiomatic: If it succeeds, the empress and the young emperor will owe you their gratitude—this is a plan without risk.

sentences.zh: 請君微說主上令粗解，珽當自外上表論之。」

translations.literal: I ask you to hint to the sovereign so that he roughly understands; Ting will from outside submit a memorial arguing it."
translations.idiomatic: Please hint at this to the emperor so he grasps the idea; I will submit a memorial from outside to press the case."

sentences.zh: 士開許諾。

translations.literal: Shikai promised.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai agreed.

sentences.zh: 會有慧星見。

translations.literal: It happened that a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: A comet then appeared.

sentences.zh: 太史奏云：「慧，除舊布新之象，當有易主。」

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer memorialized, saying, "A comet is the sign of removing the old and spreading the new; there ought to be a change of ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The grand astrologer reported, "A comet signifies sweeping away the old and ushering in the new—there will be a change of ruler."

sentences.zh: 珽於是上書言：「陛下雖為天子，未為極貴，宜傳位東宮，且以上應天道。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Ting submitted a memorial, saying, "Your Majesty, though you are Son of Heaven, are not yet in the utmost nobility; you ought to transmit the position to the Eastern Palace, and moreover thereby respond above to Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: Ting then memorialized, "Your Majesty is Son of Heaven but not yet in the highest fortune; you should abdicate to the Eastern Palace and thereby answer Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 並上魏顯祖禪子故事。

translations.literal: He also submitted precedents of how Wei Emperor Xianzu ceded the throne to his son.
translations.idiomatic: He cited as well Northern Wei's precedent of Emperor Xianzu's abdication to his son.

sentences.zh: 齊主從之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Qi followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 丙子，使太宰段韶持節奉皇帝璽綬，傳位於太子緯。

translations.literal: On bingzi, he sent Grand Preceptor Duan Shao, bearing the staff of authority, to present the imperial seal and cord and transmit the position to Crown Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he sent Grand Preceptor Duan Shao with credentials bearing the imperial seal and cord to abdicate in favor of Crown Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 太子即皇帝位於晉陽宮，大赦，改元天統。

translations.literal: The crown prince then took the emperor's position at the Jinyang Palace, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Tiantong.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took the throne at the Jinyang palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Tiantong.

sentences.zh: 又詔以太子妃斛律氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict making the crown prince's consort of the Hulu clan empress.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also named Crown Princess Hulu empress.

sentences.zh: 於是群公上世祖尊號為太上皇帝，軍國大事鹹以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon the assembled nobles advanced for Shizu the honorific title Retired Emperor; military and state great affairs were all to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: The nobles then honored Shizu as Retired Emperor; all military and civil affairs were to be reported to him.

sentences.zh: 使黃門侍郎馮子琮、尚書左丞胡長粲輔導少主，出入禁中，專典敷奏。

translations.literal: He sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Feng Zigong and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Hu Changcan to guide and instruct the young sovereign; they entered and left within the forbidden quarters and exclusively handled presenting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Feng Zigong and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Hu Changcan were assigned to guide the young emperor, moving in and out of the inner palace and handling all memorials presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 子琮，胡後之妹夫也。

translations.literal: Zigong was the empress of the Hu clan's younger sister's husband.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zigong was the husband of Empress Hu's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 祖珽拜秘書監，加儀同三司，大被親寵，見重二宮。

translations.literal: Zu Ting was appointed Director of the Secretariat, with additional title Peer of Three Departments, greatly favored with intimacy, and esteemed by both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting was made Director of the Secretariat with the additional rank of Peer of Three Departments; he won extraordinary favor and stood high in both the retired and reigning courts.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，齊以賀拔仁為太師，侯莫陳相為太保，馮翊王潤為司徒，趙郡王睿為司空，河南王孝琬為尚書令。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Qi made Heba Ren Grand Preceptor, Hou Mo Chen Xiang Grand Guardian, the Prince of Fengyi Run Minister of Education, the Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui Minister of Works, and the Prince of Henan Xiaowan Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Qi appointed Heba Ren Grand Preceptor, Hou Mo Chen Xiang Grand Guardian, Prince Run of Fengyi as Minister of Education, Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery as Minister of Works, and Prince Xiaowan of Henan as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以瀛州刺史尉粲為太尉，斛律光為大將軍，東安王婁睿為太尉，尚書僕射趙彥深為左僕射。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he made Yingzhou Governor Wei Can Grand Commandant, Hulu Guang Grand General, the Prince of Dong'an Lou Rui Grand Commandant, and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Yingzhou governor Wei Can was named Grand Commandant, Hulu Guang Grand General, Prince Lou Rui of Dong'an Grand Commandant, and Vice Director Zhao Yanshen Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 五月，突厥遣使至齊，始與齊通。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Tujue sent envoys to Qi; for the first time they communicated with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Turks sent envoys to Qi, opening relations for the first time.

sentences.zh: 六月，己巳，齊主使兼散騎常侍王季高來聘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi, the ruler of Qi sent Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Wang Jigao to come on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi, the Qi emperor sent Concurrent Regular Attendant Wang Jigao to Chen on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day xinsi, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, xinsi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 上遣都督程靈洗自鄱陽別道擊周迪，破之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Area Commander Cheng Lingxi from Poyang by a separate route to strike Zhou Di and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent area commander Cheng Lingxi from Poyang along a side route to attack Zhou Di and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 迪與麾下十餘人竄於山穴中，日月浸久，從者亦稍苦之。

translations.literal: Di with a dozen or so men under his command hid in a mountain cave; days and months gradually lengthened, and those who followed also gradually found it bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Di fled into a mountain cave with a dozen followers; as weeks turned into months, even his men began to suffer.

sentences.zh: 後遣人潛出臨川市魚鮭，臨川太守駱牙執之，令取迪自效，因使腹心勇士隨之入山。

translations.literal: Later he sent a man secretly out to Linchuan market to buy fish and dried meat; Linchuan Administrator Luo Ya seized him and ordered him to bring Di in to prove merit, whereupon he sent trusted brave warriors to follow him into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He later sent a man secretly to buy fish at Linchuan market; prefect Luo Ya seized the man and made him lead the way to capture Di, sending trusted warriors to follow him into the hills.

sentences.zh: 其人誘迪出獵，勇士伏於道旁，出斬之。

translations.literal: That man enticed Di to come out hunting; the brave warriors lay in ambush beside the road and came out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The man lured Di out on a hunt; the warriors lay in wait along the road and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，傳首至建康。

translations.literal: On bingxu, they transmitted the head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Di's head was sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，周主如秦州；

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Zhou ruler went to Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the Zhou emperor went to Qinzhou;

sentences.zh: 八月，丙子，還長安。

translations.literal: in the eighth month, on bingzi, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month, on bingzi, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 己卯，立皇子伯固為新安王，伯恭為晉安王，伯仁為廬陵王，伯義為江夏王。

translations.literal: On jimao, he established the imperial princes Bogu as Prince of Xin'an, Bogong as Prince of Jin'an, Boren as Prince of Luling, and Boyi as Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Chen enfeoffed Prince Bogu as Prince of Xin'an, Bogong as Prince of Jin'an, Boren as Prince of Luling, and Boyi as Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，周以函谷關城為通洛防，以金州刺史賀若敦為中州刺史，鎮函谷。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinhai, Zhou made the Hangu Pass city the Tongluo Defense, made Jinzhou Governor He Ruo Dun Zhongzhou Governor, and garrisoned Hangu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, on xinhai, Zhou made Hangu Pass the Tongluo garrison, appointed Jinzhou governor He Ruo Dun governor of Zhongzhou, and stationed him at Hangu.

sentences.zh: 敦恃才負氣，顧其流輩皆為大將軍，敦獨未得，兼以湘州之役，全軍而返，謂宜受賞，翻得除名，對台使出怨言。

translations.literal: Dun relied on his talent and bore himself with proud spirit; he looked back and saw that his peers were all grand generals while Dun alone had not yet received it; moreover, in the Xiangzhou campaign he returned with the whole army, and he thought he ought to receive reward—instead he was struck from the rolls, and facing the ministry offices he voiced resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was talented and proud; his peers had all been made grand generals while he alone had not, and though he had brought his army back intact from the Xiangzhou campaign, he was struck from the rolls instead of rewarded and voiced his grievance before the ministry.

sentences.zh: 晉公護怒，征還，逼令自殺。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu was angry, summoned him back, and compelled him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was enraged, recalled him, and forced him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 臨死，謂其子弼曰：「吾志平江南，今而不果，汝必成吾志。

translations.literal: Facing death, he said to his son Bi, "My ambition was to pacify the lands south of the Yangtze; now it is not achieved—you must fulfill my ambition.
translations.idiomatic: At the point of death he told his son Bi, "I meant to conquer the south; it is not done—you must finish what I began.

sentences.zh: 吾以舌死，汝不可不思。」

translations.literal: I die because of my tongue—you must not fail to reflect on this."
translations.idiomatic: I die for my tongue—never forget that."

sentences.zh: 因引錐刺弼舌出血以誡之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew an awl and pierced Bi's tongue until it bled, to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove an awl through Bi's tongue until it bled, to sear the lesson home.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸未，齊太上皇至鄴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guiwei, Qi's Retired Emperor arrived at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guiwei, the Qi retired emperor reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊世祖之為長廣王也，數為顯祖所捶，心常銜之。

translations.literal: When Qi Shizu was Prince of Changguang, he was repeatedly beaten by Emperor Xianzu and in his heart always harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu of Qi had been Prince of Changguang, Emperor Xianzu had often beaten him, and he had long borne a grudge.

sentences.zh: 顯祖每見祖珽，常呼為賊，故珽亦怨之；

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Xianzu saw Zu Ting he always called him "thief," so Ting also resented him;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu had always called Zu Ting a thief whenever he saw him, and Ting resented him as well;

sentences.zh: 且欲求媚於世祖，乃說世祖曰：「文宣狂暴，何得稱『文』？

translations.literal: moreover wishing to seek favor with Shizu, he thereupon said to Shizu, "Wenxuan was violent and fierce—how can he be called 'Wen'?
translations.idiomatic: and wishing to curry favor with Shizu, he urged him, "Wenxuan was violent and brutal—how can the character wen, 'cultured,' apply?

sentences.zh: 既非創業，何得稱『祖』？

translations.literal: Since he did not found the enterprise, how can he be called 'Ancestor'?
translations.idiomatic: He did not found the dynasty—how can he be styled 'Ancestor'?

sentences.zh: 若文宣為祖，陛下萬歲後當何所稱？」

translations.literal: If Wenxuan is made Ancestor, after Your Majesty's ten thousand years what title will you take?"
translations.idiomatic: If Wenxuan is made an ancestral temple name, what title will Your Majesty take after you pass?"

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 己丑，改謚獻武皇帝為神武皇帝，廟號高祖，獻明皇后為武明皇后。

translations.literal: On jichou, he changed the posthumous title Emperor Xianwu to Emperor Shenwu, temple name Gaozu, and Empress Xianming to Empress Wuming.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the posthumous title of Emperor Xianwu was changed to Emperor Shenwu with temple name Gaozu, and Empress Xianming was renamed Empress Wuming.

sentences.zh: 令有司更議文宣謚號。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to deliberate anew on Wenxuan's posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the authorities to reconsider Wenxuan's posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，封皇子伯禮為武陵王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, he enfeoffed the imperial prince Boli as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Prince Boli was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，齊上皇如晉陽。

translations.literal: On renxu, Qi's Retired Emperor went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Qi retired emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 庚午，齊改謚文宣皇帝為景烈皇帝，廟號威宗。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Qi changed the posthumous title Emperor Wenxuan to Emperor Jinglie, temple name Weizong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Qi changed Wenxuan's posthumous title to Emperor Jinglie with temple name Weizong.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己卯，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jimao, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, on jimao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸未，周大赦，改元天和。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Zhou proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the era name to Tianhe.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Northern Zhou proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Tianhe.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，齊主祀圜丘；

translations.literal: On xinmao, the ruler of Qi sacrificed at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Qi emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，祫太廟。

translations.literal: on guisi, he performed the he sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: on guisi he performed the he joint sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 丙申，齊以吏部尚書尉瑾為右僕射。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Qi made Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wei Jin Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Qi appointed Minister of Personnel Wei Jin as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 己亥，周主耕藉田。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Zhou ruler plowed the ceremonial field.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Zhou emperor performed the ceremonial plowing at the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 庚子，齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the ruler of Qi went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 周遣小載師杜杲來聘。

translations.literal: Zhou sent Lesser Master of Carriages Du Guo to come on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent Lesser Master of Carriages Du Guo on a diplomatic visit to Chen.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚戌，齊上皇還鄴。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengxu, Qi's Retired Emperor returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu, the Qi retired emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 丙子，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On bingzi, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Chen proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 三月，己卯，以安成王頊為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jimao, he made the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jimao, Prince Xu of Ancheng was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 丙午，周主祀南郊。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Zhou emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，大雩。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, a great rain prayer was held.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, the court held a great rain prayer.

sentences.zh: 上不豫，台閣眾事，並令尚書僕射到仲舉、五兵尚書孔奐共決之。

translations.literal: The emperor was unwell; all affairs of the terrace offices were together ordered to be decided by Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju and Minister of the Five Armies Kong Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell ill and entrusted all government business to Vice Director Dao Zhongju and Minister of the Five Armies Kong Huan.

sentences.zh: 奐，琇之之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Huan was the great-grandson of Xiu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan was a great-grandson of Kong Xiu.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，奐、仲舉與司空、尚書令、揚州刺史安成王頊、吏部尚書袁樞、中書舍人劉師知入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the illness was severe, Huan, Zhongju, together with Minister of Works, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Yangzhou Inspector the Prince of Ancheng Xu, Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu, and Palace Secretariat Attendant Liu Shizhi entered to attend medicine.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, Huan and Zhongju were joined at his bedside by Minister of Works and Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Xu of Ancheng, Yangzhou inspector, Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu, and Palace Secretariat Attendant Liu Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 樞，君正之子也。

translations.literal: Shu was the son of Junzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was a son of Yuan Junzheng.

sentences.zh: 太子伯宗柔弱，上憂其不能守位，謂頊曰：「吾欲遵太伯之事。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Bozong was weak and mild; the emperor worried that he could not hold the position and said to Xu, "I wish to follow Taibo's affair."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Bozong was frail, and the emperor, fearing he could not hold the throne, told Xu, "I mean to follow the example of Taibo."

sentences.zh: 頊拜伏泣涕，固辭。

translations.literal: Xu bowed prostrate, weeping with tears, and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xu prostrated himself, weeping, and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 上又謂仲舉、奐等曰：「今三方鼎峙，四海事重，宜須長居。

translations.literal: The emperor again said to Zhongju, Huan, and the others, "Now the three sides stand like a tripod; affairs of the four seas are weighty—you ought to dwell long in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told Zhongju, Huan, and the others, "With three powers contending and the realm at stake, you must remain in office.

sentences.zh: 騰欲近則晉成，遠隆殷法，卿等宜遵此意。」

translations.literal: If you wish to be near, then follow Jin Cheng; if far, exalt the Yin method—you ought to follow this intent."
translations.idiomatic: If you stay close, follow the model of Jin Cheng; if you step back, honor the Yin precedent—you must heed this intent."

sentences.zh: 孔奐流涕對曰：「陛下御膳違和，痊復非久。

translations.literal: Kong Huan, with tears streaming, replied, "Your Majesty's imperial meal is out of harmony; recovery will not be long.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan answered through tears, "Your Majesty's ailment is slight; you will recover soon.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為鼎盛，聖德日躋。

translations.literal: The crown prince is in the fullness of youth; sagely virtue daily ascends.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is in his prime and grows in virtue daily.

sentences.zh: 安成王介弟之尊，足為周旦。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ancheng, in the honored status of a younger brother by a concubine, is sufficient to be the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xu of Ancheng, as a younger brother of the blood, can serve as the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 若有廢立之心，臣等愚，誠不敢聞詔。」

translations.literal: If there is a mind to depose and establish, we your subjects are foolish and truly dare not hear such an edict."
translations.idiomatic: If you harbor any thought of deposing the heir, we your servants are too dull to obey such an order."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「古之遺直，復見於卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The straight remnant of antiquity is seen again in you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The upright ministers of old live again in you."

sentences.zh: 乃以奐為太子詹事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Huan Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Kong Huan Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：夫臣之事君，宜將順其美，正救其惡。

translations.literal: Chen Guang remarks: In a subject's service to his ruler, he ought to nurture and follow the ruler's virtues and straightly remedy his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: A minister serving his sovereign should nurture what is good in him and correct what is evil.

sentences.zh: 孔奐在陳，處腹心之重任，決禮義之大計，苟以世祖之言為不誠，則當如竇嬰面辯，袁盎廷爭，防微杜漸以絕覬覦之心。

translations.literal: Kong Huan in Chen held a trusted post at the ruler's heart and decided great questions of ritual and righteousness; if he took Shizu's words as insincere, then he ought, like Dou Ying, to argue face to face, or like Yuan Ang, to contend in court—to stop evil at the sprout and cut off covetous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan in Chen occupied a position of deepest trust and weighed the gravest questions of ritual and right. If he believed Emperor Wendi's intent was false, he should have remonstrated as Dou Ying did in open debate, or as Yuan Ang did at court—stopping the rot early and cutting off all who would plot usurpation.

sentences.zh: 以為誠邪，則當請明下詔書，宣告中外，使世祖有宋宣之美，高宗無楚靈之惡。

translations.literal: If he thought them sincere, then he ought to request a clear proclamation, announcing it within and without, so that Shizu might have the beauty of Duke Xuan of Song, and Gaozong would lack the evil of King Ling of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: If he took the emperor at his word, he should have asked for a clear edict proclaimed at home and abroad, so that Wendi would gain the praise owed Duke Xuan of Song and the court would not repeat the evil of King Ling of Chu.

sentences.zh: 不然，謂太子嫡嗣，不可動搖，欲保附而安全之，則當盡忠竭節，以死繼之，如晉之荀息，趙之肥義。

translations.literal: Otherwise, holding that the crown prince as legitimate heir could not be shaken, wishing to preserve and attach himself and win safety, then he ought to exhaust loyalty and drain his integrity, following in death, like Xun Xi of Jin or Fei Yi of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Or, if he held the heir's position inviolable and wished only to cling to power in safety, he should have given his utmost loyalty unto death, as Xun Xi of Jin or Fei Yi of Zhao did.

sentences.zh: 奈何於君之存，則逆探其情而求合焉；

translations.literal: Yet how was it that while the ruler still lived, he inversely probed his feelings to seek accord?
translations.idiomatic: Yet while the emperor still lived, he probed obliquely for the ruler's hidden wishes and strove to conform to them.

sentences.zh: 及其既沒，則權臣移國而不能救，嗣主失位而不能死！

translations.literal: When he had already died, powerful ministers shifted the realm yet he could not rescue it; the heir lost his place yet he could not die for it!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was gone, powerful ministers seized the state and he could not save it; the rightful heir was dethroned and he would not die in his defense!

sentences.zh: 斯乃奸諛之尤者，而世祖謂之遺直，以托六尺之孤，豈不悖哉！

translations.literal: This is the extreme of flattery and deceit—yet Shizu called him a straight remnant of antiquity and entrusted to him a six-foot orphan: is this not perverse!
translations.idiomatic: Here was flattery at its worst—yet Emperor Wendi called him a minister straight as those of old and entrusted to him his young son: how perverse!

sentences.zh: 癸酉，上殂。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 上起自艱難，知民疾苦。

translations.literal: The emperor had risen from hardship and knew the people's toil and suffering.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen through hardship and knew the people's sufferings firsthand.

sentences.zh: 性明察儉約，每夜刺閨取外事分判者，前後相續。

translations.literal: By nature he was perspicacious and frugal; each night those who pierced the side apartments to take outside affairs for him to divide and judge came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Keen-eyed and frugal by nature, he would have officials slip reports through the side door nightly for him to review; attendants bearing such papers kept coming without cease.

sentences.zh: 敕傳更簽於殿中者，必投簽於階石之上，令鎗然有聲，曰：「吾雖眠，亦令驚覺。」

translations.literal: He ordered those who changed the watch and delivered tally-slips in the hall necessarily to cast the slips onto the step stones so they rang out sharply, saying: "Though I sleep, I still wish to be startled awake."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the night watchmen in the hall to cast their tally sticks onto the stone steps so they rang sharply, saying, "Even in sleep I mean to stay alert."

sentences.zh: 太子即位，大赦。

translations.literal: The crown prince took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended the throne and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，己卯，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰後太后。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jimao, the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager, and the empress as queen dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jimao, the empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager and the empress to queen dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，齊以兼尚書左僕射武興王普為尚書令。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Qi made the concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Wuxing Pu, Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Northern Qi appointed Prince Pu of Wuxing, who had been serving concurrently as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾龍涸王莫昌帥部落附於周，以其地為扶州。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Prince Longhu Mobo led his tribes to submit to Zhou, and his lands were made Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo, king of Longhu in Tuyuhun, led his tribes to submit to Zhou; their territory was organized as Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以安成王頊為驃騎大將軍、司徒、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Prince of Ancheng Xu was made General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Prince Xu of Ancheng was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Education, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and supreme commander of all military forces.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司徐度為司空，以吏部尚書袁樞為左僕射，吳興太守沈欽為右僕射，御史中丞徐陵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the General of the Central Army, Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies Xu Du, was made Minister of Works; the Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Shu was made Left Vice Director; the Administrator of Wuxing Shen Qin was made Right Vice Director; and the Attending Investigator Xu Ling was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Xu Du, Grand General of the Central Army and commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies, was named Minister of Works; Yuan Shu, director of the Ministry of Personnel, became Left Vice Director; Shen Qin, governor of Wuxing, Right Vice Director; and Xu Ling, attending investigator, director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 陵以梁末以來，選授多濫，乃為書示眾曰：「梁元帝承侯景之凶荒，王太尉接荊州之禍敗，故使官方，窮此紛雜。

translations.literal: Xu Ling, because since the end of Liang appointments had been largely excessive, then composed a letter to show the assembly, saying: "Emperor Yuan of Liang inherited Hou Jing's savage desolation; Wang the Grand Commandant received Jingzhou's calamity and defeat—therefore official ranks fell into such confusion and entanglement.
translations.idiomatic: Finding appointments grossly lax since the late Liang, Xu Ling circulated a letter to the bureaucracy: "After Hou Jing's ravages, Emperor Yuan of Liang inherited a ruined realm; when Wang the Grand Commandant took Jingzhou, disaster compounded disaster—small wonder that official ranks fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 永安之時，聖朝草創，白銀難得，黃札易營，權以官階，代於錢絹。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an period, the sacred court was just being founded; white silver was hard to obtain, yellow documents were easy to secure—for a time official grades stood in for money and silk.
