translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era, as our dynasty was being founded, silver was scarce but appointment edicts were easy to obtain; for a time office rank substituted for cash and silk.

sentences.zh: 致令員外、常侍，路上比肩，咨議、參軍，市中無數，豈是朝章固應如此！

translations.literal: This caused extra-grade attendants and chamberlains to walk shoulder to shoulder on the roads, consultants and staff officers to swarm the markets beyond count: could court regulations properly be such as this!
translations.idiomatic: Extra-grade attendants and chamberlains crowded the streets shoulder to shoulder; consultants and staff officers thronged the markets beyond counting—was this how the court ought to look!

sentences.zh: 今衣冠禮樂，日富年華，何可猶作舊意，非理望也！」

translations.literal: Now caps and robes, ritual and music, daily grow richer and years more splendid—how can one still hold to the old ways? This is not what reason and expectation demand!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that ritual and refinement grow richer year by year, how can we cling to old abuses? It is neither reasonable nor to be hoped for!"

sentences.zh: 眾鹹服之。

translations.literal: The assembly all submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: All present assented.

sentences.zh: 己亥，齊立上皇子弘為齊安王，仁固為北平王，仁英為高平王，仁光為淮南王。

translations.literal: On jihai, Qi established the emperor's son Hong as Prince of Qi'an, Rengu as Prince of Beiping, Renying as Prince of Gaoping, and Renguang as Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Northern Qi enfeoffed the emperor's sons: Hong as Prince of Qi'an, Rengu as Prince of Beiping, Renying of Gaoping, and Renguang of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 六月，齊遣兼散騎常侍韋道儒來聘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Qi sent the concurrent Master of Regular Attendance Wei Daoru on a mission of friendly inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Northern Qi sent Wei Daoru, concurrent Master of Regular Attendance, as envoy on a goodwill mission.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，葬文皇帝於永寧陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: On bingyin, they buried the Cultivated Emperor at Yongning Mausoleum; his temple name was Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Emperor Wen was buried at Yongning Mausoleum; his temple name was Shizu.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，周築武功等諸城以置軍士。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, Zhou built Wugong and other walled cities to station troops.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, Northern Zhou fortified Wugong and other cities to garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，立妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the consort Lady Wang was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Consort Wang was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 八月，齊上皇如晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the retired emperor of Qi went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Northern Qi retired emperor traveled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 周信州蠻冉令賢、向五子王等據巴峽反，攻陷白帝，黨與連結二千餘里。

translations.literal: Zhou's Xinzhou barbarians Ran Lingxian, Xiang Wuzi Wang, and others held the Ba Gorge and rebelled, storming and taking Baidi; their partisans linked for more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's Xinzhou, the chieftains Ran Lingxian and Xiang Wuzi Wang seized the Ba Gorge and rebelled, capturing Baidi; their allies stretched along more than two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 周遣開府儀同三司元契、趙剛等前後討之，終不克。

translations.literal: Zhou sent commissioners with equal protocol Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and others, in successive campaigns to attack them, but in the end could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou dispatched Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and other commissioners of equal protocol in successive campaigns, but could not subdue them.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔開府儀同三司陸騰督開府儀同三司王亮、司馬裔討之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered Commissioner Lu Teng to supervise Commissioners Wang Liang and Sima Yi in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, an edict put Commissioner Lu Teng in overall command of Wang Liang and Sima Yi to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 騰軍於湯口，令賢於江南據險要，置十城，遠結涔陽蠻為聲援，自帥精卒固守水邏城。

translations.literal: Teng encamped at Tangkou; Lingxian on the southern bank held strategic points, set up ten cities, distantly linked the Cenyang barbarians as supporting voices, and himself led crack troops to defend Shuibicheng steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng pitched camp at Tangkou. Lingxian held the south bank's passes, fortified ten cities, and won distant support from the Cenyang tribes while he himself led elite troops in a stubborn defense of Shuibicheng.

sentences.zh: 騰召諸將問計，皆欲先取水邏，後攻江南。

translations.literal: Teng summoned the generals to ask plans; all wished first to take Shuibi, then attack the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Teng called his commanders to council; all favored taking Shuibicheng first, then the southern bank.

sentences.zh: 騰曰：「令賢內恃水邏金湯之固，外托涔陽輔車之援。

translations.literal: Teng said: "Lingxian within relies on Shuibi's metal-and-water solidity; without, he leans on Cenyang's cart-and-axle mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: Teng said, "Lingxian trusts in Shuibicheng's impregnable walls within and in Cenyang's mutual aid without.

sentences.zh: 資糧充實，器械精新。

translations.literal: Provisions and grain are full and solid; weapons and gear are refined and new.
translations.idiomatic: His stores are full and his arms sharp and new.

sentences.zh: 以我懸軍，攻其嚴壘，脫一戰不克，更成其氣。

translations.literal: With our army isolated deep in enemy territory, attacking his stern ramparts—if one battle fails, we only strengthen his morale.
translations.idiomatic: We are deep in enemy country, striking a fortified line; if even one assault fails, we will only stiffen his resolve.

sentences.zh: 不如頓軍湯口，先取江南，剪其羽毛，然後進軍水邏，此制勝之術也。」

translations.literal: Better to halt the army at Tangkou, first take the south bank, trim his feathers, then advance on Shuibi—this is the art of securing victory."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold at Tangkou, seize the south bank first and clip his wings, then march on Shuibicheng—that is how to win."

sentences.zh: 乃遣王亮帥眾渡江，旬日，拔其八城，捕虜及納降各千計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Wang Liang to lead the host across the river; within ten days they stormed eight of his cities; captives taken and those who surrendered numbered about a thousand each.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Wang Liang across the river; within ten days eight cities fell, with roughly a thousand captives and a thousand surrendering in each case.

sentences.zh: 遂間募驍勇，數道進攻水邏。

translations.literal: He then recruited the boldest warriors from among them and attacked Shuibi by several routes.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited the fiercest fighters and pressed Shuibicheng along several axes.

sentences.zh: 蠻帥冉伯犁、冉安西素與令賢有仇，騰說誘，賂以金帛，使為鄉導。

translations.literal: The barbarian chiefs Ran Boli and Ran Anxi had long borne enmity toward Lingxian; Teng persuaded and enticed them, bribing them with gold and silk to serve as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains Ran Boli and Ran Anxi had long hated Lingxian; Teng won them over with gold and silk and made them his guides.

sentences.zh: 水邏之旁有石勝城，令賢使其兄子龍真據之。

translations.literal: Beside Shuibi was Shisheng City; Lingxian sent his elder brother's son Longzhen to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Near Shuibicheng stood Shisheng; Lingxian entrusted it to his nephew Longzhen.

sentences.zh: 騰密誘龍真，龍真遂以城降。

translations.literal: Teng secretly enticed Longzhen, and Longzhen thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Teng secretly won over Longzhen, who then surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 水邏眾潰，斬首萬餘級，捕虜萬餘口。

translations.literal: Shuibi's host collapsed; more than ten thousand heads were cut; more than ten thousand mouths were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison of Shuibicheng broke; more than ten thousand heads were taken and more than ten thousand people captured alive.

sentences.zh: 令賢走，追獲，斬之。

translations.literal: Lingxian fled, was pursued and captured, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxian fled, was overtaken, and executed.

sentences.zh: 騰積骸於水邏城側為京觀，是後群蠻望之，輒大哭，不敢復叛。

translations.literal: Teng heaped corpses beside Shuibi City into a jingguan mound; thereafter when the various barbarians beheld it, they invariably wept loudly and did not dare rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Teng built a corpse mound from the dead beside Shuibicheng; thereafter the tribes would burst into tears at the sight and dared not rebel again.

sentences.zh: 向五子王據石黑城，使其子寶勝據雙城。

translations.literal: Xiang Wuzi Wang held Shihei City and sent his son Baosheng to hold Shuangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Wuzi Wang held Shihei and stationed his son Baosheng at Shuangcheng.

sentences.zh: 水邏既平，騰頻遣諭之，猶不下。

translations.literal: Once Shuibi was pacified, Teng repeatedly sent envoys to instruct him, yet he still would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuibicheng fell, Teng sent repeated envoys to summon him, but he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 進擊，皆擒之，盡斬諸向酋長，捕虜萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack, he captured them all, beheaded all the Xiang chieftains, and took captive more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng attacked, took them both, executed every Xiang chieftain, and captured more than ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 信州舊治白帝，騰徙之於八陳灘北，以司馬裔為信州刺史。

translations.literal: Xinzhou's old seat was at Baidi; Teng moved it north of Bachan Beach and made Sima Yi Governor of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Teng moved the Xinzhou seat from Baidi to north of the Eight Formations Shoals and appointed Sima Yi governor.

sentences.zh: 小吏部隴西辛昂，奉使梁、益，且為騰督軍糧。

translations.literal: Junior Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Longxi's Xin Ang, was on a mission to Liang and Yi, and moreover supervised military grain for Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ang of Longxi, junior director in the Ministry of Personnel, was on mission to Liang and Yi and also supervised grain for Lu Teng's army.

sentences.zh: 時臨、信、楚、合等州民多眾亂，昂諭以禍福，赴者如歸。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other prefectures were many in disorder; Ang instructed them with misfortune and fortune, and those who came did so as returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Many districts of Lin, Xin, Chu, and He were in turmoil; Ang preached consequences to them, and people flocked to him as to their homes.

sentences.zh: 乃令老弱負糧，壯夫拒戰，鹹樂為用。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the old and weak to carry grain and the strong to resist in battle, and all gladly served.
translations.idiomatic: He set the old and weak to carry grain and the able-bodied to fight, and all served willingly.

sentences.zh: 使還，會巴州萬榮郡民反，攻圍郡城，遏絕山路。

translations.literal: On his return journey, he encountered Wanrong Commandery of Bazhou in revolt, attacking and besieging the commandery seat, cutting off mountain routes.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he found the people of Wanrong in Bazhou in revolt, besieging the prefectural city and blocking the mountain roads.

sentences.zh: 昂謂其徒曰：「凶狡猖狂，若待上聞，孤城必陷。

translations.literal: Ang said to his followers: "They are violent and cunning, running wild; if we wait for word from above, the isolated city will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: Ang told his men, "These rebels are fierce and frantic; if we wait for word from the capital, the lone city will fall.

sentences.zh: 苟利百姓，專之可也。」

translations.literal: If it benefits the people, seizing authority is permissible."
translations.idiomatic: If the people will benefit, we may take command on our own authority."

sentences.zh: 遂募通、開二州，得三千人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited from Tong and Kai prefectures and obtained three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He raised three thousand men from Tong and Kai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 倍道兼行，出其不意，直趣賊壘。

translations.literal: Traveling double marches, he struck where they did not expect and went straight to the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: He marched at double speed, took them by surprise, and struck straight at the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 賊以為大軍至，望風瓦解，一郡獲全。

translations.literal: The rebels thought a great army had arrived; at sight of the wind they dissolved, and the whole commandery was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought a great army had come; at his approach they scattered, and the whole commandery was saved.

sentences.zh: 周朝嘉之，以為渠州刺史。

translations.literal: The Zhou court praised him and made him Governor of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court rewarded him with appointment as governor of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，齊以侯莫陳相為大傅，任城王湝為太保，婁睿為大司馬，馮翊王潤為太尉，開府儀同三司韓祖念為司徒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Qi made Hou Mo Chen Xiang Grand Tutor, the Prince of Rencheng Hui Grand Guardian, Lou Rui Grand Marshal, the Prince of Fengyi Run Grand Commandant, and Commissioner Han Zunian Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Northern Qi appointed Hou Mo Chen Xiang Grand Tutor, Prince Hui of Rencheng Grand Guardian, Lou Rui Grand Marshal, Prince Run of Fengyi Grand Commandant, and Commissioner Han Zunian Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝享太廟。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the emperor offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the emperor sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙亥，周遣使來吊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Zhou sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Zhou sent envoys to offer condolences on the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，周主行視武功等新城；

translations.literal: On bingxu, the Zhou ruler went forth to inspect Wugong and other new cities;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the Zhou emperor toured the new fortifications at Wugong and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，還長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 齊河間王孝琬怨執政，為草人而射之。

translations.literal: Qi's Prince of Hejian Xiaowan resented those in power and made a straw man to shoot at.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaowan of Hejian in Qi, resenting the ruling clique, made a straw figure and shot arrows at it.

sentences.zh: 和士開、祖珽譖之於上皇曰：「草人以擬聖躬也。

translations.literal: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him to the retired emperor, saying: "The straw man is meant to represent the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai and Zu Ting denounced him to the retired emperor: "The straw figure is meant to stand in for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 又，前突厥至并州，孝琬脫兜鍪抵地，云：『我豈老嫗，須著此物！』

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Turks had previously reached Bingzhou, Xiaowan flung his helmet to the ground, saying: "Am I some old woman, that I must wear this thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Further, when the Turks had reached Bingzhou, Xiaowan threw his helmet to the ground and cried, "Do I look like some old woman to need this thing on my head!"

sentences.zh: 此言屬大家也。

translations.literal: This remark is addressed to the great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: That was aimed at all of us.

sentences.zh: 又，魏世謠言：『河南種穀河北生，白楊樹端金雞鳴。』

translations.literal: Moreover, a Wei-era rhyme runs: "Grain is sown south of the River but grows north of it; at the tip of a white poplar a golden cock crows."
translations.idiomatic: And a prophetic rhyme from Wei runs: "Grain sowed south of the River sprouts north of it; on a white poplar's crown a golden cock crows."

sentences.zh: 河南、北者，河間也。

translations.literal: South of the River" and "north" refer to Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Here, 'South' and 'north' mean Hejian.

sentences.zh: 孝琬將建金雞大赦耳。」

translations.literal: Xiaowan is about to set up a golden cock and proclaim a general amnesty, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan means to set up a golden cock and declare a general amnesty."

sentences.zh: 上皇頗惑之。

translations.literal: The retired emperor was quite swayed.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor was much persuaded.

sentences.zh: 會孝琬得佛牙，置第內，夜有光。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiaowan obtained a Buddha tooth-relic and placed it in his residence; at night it gave forth light.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan had come into possession of a Buddha relic and kept it in his mansion; by night it shone with light.

sentences.zh: 上皇聞之，使搜之，得填庫槊幡數百。

translations.literal: The retired emperor heard of it and sent men to search; they obtained several hundred spears and banners stored in armories.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor heard, he ordered a search and found hundreds of spears and banners packed in storerooms.

sentences.zh: 上皇以為反具，收訊。

translations.literal: The retired emperor deemed these equipment for rebellion and seized and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: He took these as proof of rebellion and had Xiaowan arrested and interrogated.

sentences.zh: 諸姬有陳氏者，無寵，誣孝琬云：「孝琬常畫陛下像而哭之。」

translations.literal: Among the concubines was one of the Chen clan, without favor; she falsely accused Xiaowan, saying: "Xiaowan often painted Your Majesty's likeness and wept before it."
translations.idiomatic: A concubine surnamed Chen, out of favor, falsely accused him: "Xiaowan often painted Your Majesty's portrait and wept before it."

sentences.zh: 其實世宗像也。

translations.literal: In fact it was Emperor Shizong's likeness.
translations.idiomatic: In fact it had been Prince Shizong's portrait.

sentences.zh: 上皇怒，使武衛赫連輔玄倒鞭撾之。

translations.literal: The retired emperor was enraged and had the Martial Guardsman Helian Fuyuan flog him with an inverted whip.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor in rage had Helian Fuyuan of the Martial Guard beat him with a reversed whip.

sentences.zh: 孝琬呼叔，上皇曰：「何敢呼我為叔！」

translations.literal: Xiaowan cried "Uncle!" The retired emperor said: "How dare you call me uncle!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan cried, "Uncle!" The retired emperor roared, "How dare you call me uncle!"

sentences.zh: 孝琬曰：「臣神武皇帝嫡孫，文襄皇帝嫡子，魏孝靜皇帝之甥，何為不得呼叔！」

translations.literal: Xiaowan said: "Your subject is the legitimate grandson of Emperor Shenwu, the legitimate son of Emperor Wenxiang, and the nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei—why may I not call you uncle!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan answered: "I am the eldest grandson of Gao Huan, eldest son of Gao Cheng, and nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei—why may I not call you uncle!"

sentences.zh: 上皇愈怒，折其兩脛而死。

translations.literal: The retired emperor grew still angrier and broke both his shins, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor only grew angrier, snapped both his lower legs, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 安德王延宗哭之，淚赤。

translations.literal: Prince Ande Yanzong wept for him until his tears ran red.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yanzong of Ande mourned him until his tears ran red.

sentences.zh: 又為草人，鞭而訊之曰：「何故殺我兄！」

translations.literal: He again made a straw man, flogged it, and interrogated it, saying: "Why did you kill my elder brother!"
translations.idiomatic: He made another straw figure, beat it, and cried to it: "Why did you kill my brother!"

sentences.zh: 奴告之，上皇覆延宗於地，馬鞭鞭之二百，幾死。

translations.literal: A slave reported it; the retired emperor threw Yanzong to the ground and lashed him two hundred strokes with a riding crop, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: A servant betrayed him. The retired emperor threw Yanzong to the floor and gave him two hundred strokes of the riding crop, nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊賜侍中、中書監元文遙姓高氏，頃之，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: That year, Qi bestowed on Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Overseer of the Secretariat Yuan Wenyao the surname Gao; shortly thereafter he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qi granted Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Wenyao, also Grand Overseer of the Secretariat, the surname Gao; soon after he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 魏末以來，縣令多用廝役，由是士流恥為之。

translations.literal: Since the end of Wei, county magistrates were largely drawn from bond servants; for this reason the gentry were ashamed to serve in such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Wei, county magistrates had often been bond servants, and gentlemen declined such office in shame.

sentences.zh: 文遙以為縣令治民之本，遂請革選，密擇貴遊子弟，發敕用之；

translations.literal: Wenyao held that the county magistrate was the root of governing the people; he then requested to reform selection, secretly choosing sons of noble houses, and issued edicts to appoint them;
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao held that the magistrate was the foundation of rule over the people and petitioned for reform, quietly selecting sons of eminent families and issuing edicts to appoint them;

sentences.zh: 猶恐其披訴、悉召之集神武門，令趙郡王睿宣旨唱名，厚加尉諭而遣之。

translations.literal: Still fearing they might file appeals of grievance, he summoned them all to assemble at the Shenwu Gate, had the Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui proclaim the imperial will and call their names, richly comforted and instructed them, and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Lest they appeal against the appointments, he summoned them all to Shenwu Gate, had Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery read the imperial order and call each name, reassured them warmly, and sent them to their posts.

sentences.zh: 齊之士人為縣自此始。

translations.literal: From this time gentlemen of Qi served as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: From that time gentlemen of Qi began to hold county magistracies.
